job.title: 1st Shift - Quality Technician
job.description:
Quality Technician
Location: Three Rivers Shift: 1st shift Mon-Thursday 6am-4pm Pay: $20.00 per hour
Job Summary
Are you detail-oriented and committed to accuracy? We’re seeking a Quality Technician to join our team in Three Rivers, MI. In this role, you’ll play a key part in ensuring products meet quality standards before they reach customers. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys hands-on inspection work, follows procedures closely, and takes pride in maintaining high-quality results in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
What You’ll Be Doing
As a Quality Technician, your core responsibilities will include:
? Inspecting products and materials: Perform visual, dimensional, and functional inspections to ensure compliance with customer and company specifications. ? Using measurement tools: Work with calipers, micrometers, gauges, and other inspection equipment to verify product accuracy. ? Documenting results: Record inspection findings, complete quality reports, and communicate issues to supervisors or production leads. ? Identifying defects: Detect nonconforming parts, tag or quarantine defective items, and assist with root-cause information when needed. ? Supporting production: Work closely with machine operators and assemblers to maintain consistent quality throughout the manufacturing process. ? Maintaining a clean and safe work area: Follow all safety procedures, handle materials properly, and support general housekeeping tasks.
In addition, you may assist with incoming material checks, final inspections, rework verification, and other quality-related tasks as needed.
What We’re Looking For
Qualifications:
? Previous experience in quality inspection, manufacturing, or assembly preferred but not required. ? Ability to read and understand basic work instructions, diagrams, or blueprints.
? Ability to use basic measurement tools (calipers, gauges, rulers, etc.). ? Quality Tools, PPAP, APQP, MSA, PFMEA
? Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
? Ability to stand for long periods and lift up to 40 lbs. ? ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management System
? Dependable attendance and a strong work ethic.
? Willingness to work in a fast-paced, manufacturing environment.
Skills:
? Attention to Detail: Critical for identifying defects and ensuring product consistency.
? Communication: Ability to clearly report issues and collaborate with production teams. ? Problem-Solving: Helps identify quality concerns and support corrective actions.
? Basic Mechanical Aptitude: Useful for understanding how parts fit, function, and meet specifications.
Why Join Us?
This is an excellent opportunity for both short-term and long-term employment. We are committed to providing a supportive work environment and opportunities for growth within quality, production, and manufacturing operations.

job.title: 3rd Shift - Material Handler
job.description:
The Manufacturing Material Handler is responsible for supplying raw materials to production work cells and moving finished goods to proper warehouse bin location. This position also supports general warehouse functions such as loading and unloading trucks and moving items to proper location.
Essential Functions and Responsibilities: * Safely utilizes a powered industrial truck to supply production cells with needed raw materials to meet production demands. * Shrink wraps, inspects, and delivers finished orders to proper warehouse bin locations.* Utilizes scanning system meticulously to track movement of product throughout different movements. * Notifies production supervisor or supply chain department of inventory discrepancies. *Follows bill of materials to correctly stage batching supplies for batch tenders. *Collaborates with packagers on correct raw materials needed to complete work orders. * Load and unload trucks as called upon by the shipping and receiving department. * Ensures clean work environment including sweeping and cleaning work areas. * Provides back-up assistance to other production positions as needed. * Complies with all safety, health, and regulatory compliance laws and policies. * Other duties/tasks as assigned by supervisor.
Minimum Qualifications:
* High school diploma or GED is preferred, or 3 months of related experience and/or training, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. * A demonstrated ability to read and follow formulas and instructions. * Must have ability to obtain powered industrial truck permit and safely operate a powered industrial truck. * This position required the physical capability to wear and safely utilize a respirator during certain essential functions.
Working Conditions and/or Physical Demands: * Must regularly lift and/or move up to ten pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to fifty pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move more than one hundred pounds. * Frequently required to stand, walk, stoop, knee, and crouch.

Location: Bristol, IN Shift: 1st Shift – 5:45 AM–2:15 PM, Monday–Friday Pay: $19.00 per hour Job Summary
Are you highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable working in a fast-paced manufacturing environment? We're seeking a Kitter to join our team in Bristol, IN. In this role, you'll be responsible for accurately preparing customer orders by gathering large quantities of parts, packaging them into bundles, and preparing completed orders for shipment. This is a hands-on position that combines physical material handling with computer work and requires extreme attention to detail to ensure every order is complete and accurate.
What You’ll Be Doing
As a Kitter, your core responsibilities will include: -Order Preparation: Pull and organize customer orders containing large quantities of parts, typically totaling 1,000–2,000 pounds per job. -Bundling & Packaging: Accurately package parts into bundles, typically in quantities of two, while ensuring each order is prepared according to specifications. -Sundry Items: Use computer systems to identify orders requiring additional sundry items and determine the correct quantity of parts to add to each shipment. -Pallet Preparation: Once orders are completely packaged, secure sundry items to the pallet and prepare the finished order for shipment. -Production Efficiency: Complete approximately 3–5 jobs per day, depending on the size and complexity of each order, while maintaining accuracy and quality.
In addition, you will also be expected to maintain an organized work area, communicate any discrepancies or issues, and work efficiently with the production and shipping teams.
What We’re Looking For
To be successful in this role, you should have the following: Qualifications: Ability to handle and move large quantities of parts throughout the workday Ability to work with orders weighing approximately 1,000–2,000 pounds in total Ability to work in a fast-paced production environment Strong attention to detail and accuracy Basic computer skills and ability to use computer systems to review orders Ability to accurately follow order and packaging instructions Reliable attendance and punctuality Ability to work Monday–Friday on 1st shift Skills: -Attention to Detail: Able to carefully review orders and ensure the correct parts and quantities are included. -Organization: Able to keep large orders, bundles, and additional items organized throughout the packaging process. -Computer Skills: Comfortable using a computer to identify order requirements and determine which sundry items need to be included. -Time Management: Able to efficiently complete multiple jobs throughout the workday while maintaining accuracy. -Problem Solving: Able to identify discrepancies or missing items and communicate issues appropriately. -Teamwork: Works well with coworkers and other departments to keep orders moving toward shipment.
What We’re Looking For in a Candidate
The ideal candidate is extremely detail-oriented, organized, dependable, and able to work with a sense of urgency. This position is a great fit for someone who can balance physical work with computer-based order information while maintaining accuracy. Because each job may involve thousands of pounds of material and multiple components, the ability to stay focused and organized throughout the entire process is essential.
Work Environment
This is a hands-on manufacturing and shipping environment where employees will spend much of the day moving, packaging, bundling, and preparing parts for shipment. The position involves handling large quantities of material and working at a consistent pace to meet daily production and shipping requirements. Candidates should be comfortable with physical work and maintaining attention to detail in a fast-paced setting.

Ability to work in a team based environment

job.title: Grinder 3rd
job.description: Grinder Location: Brighton, MI Shift: 1st, 2nd, or 3rd Available Pay: Based on Experience Job Summary Are you an experienced Grinder looking for an opportunity to work in a precision machining environment? We are seeking a skilled Grinder to join our team in Brighton, MI. In this role, you will be responsible for setting up and operating OD grinding machines to produce precision components while maintaining tight tolerances and meeting customer specifications. The ideal candidate has experience with manual grinding machines, strong attention to detail, and a commitment to producing high-quality work. What You'll Be Doing As a Grinder, your core responsibilities will include: Set up and operate manual OD grinding machines according to blueprints and work specifications. Inspect finished parts using precision measuring tools such as micrometers, calipers, and indicators to verify dimensions and surface finish. Document production activities, inspections, and material usage. Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment while following all safety procedures and PPE requirements. Collaborate with team members to meet production schedules and quality expectations. Perform additional duties as assigned. What We're Looking For To be successful in this role, you should have the following: Qualifications: High School Diploma or GED required. Previous experience operating manual OD grinding machines required. Strong knowledge of grinding techniques, tooling, and materials. Ability to read and interpret blueprints, technical drawings, and work instructions. Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. and stand for extended periods throughout the shift. Skills: Experience using precision measuring tools including micrometers, calipers, and indicators. Strong mechanical aptitude and troubleshooting skills. Excellent attention to detail with the ability to maintain tight tolerances. Basic knowledge of machine maintenance and equipment care. Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. Strong communication and organizational skills. Why Join Us? This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing precision machining team where your skills will be valued and developed. You'll work in a professional manufacturing environment with opportunities for long-term growth and advancement. This position plays an important role in maintaining accurate inventory, supporting production, and ensuring materials are available when needed. The ideal candidate is organized, safety-focused, mechanically inclined, and comfortable working in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. What You’ll Be Doing Safely operate a Hi-Lo/forklift to move and stage raw materials, finished goods, packaging, tooling, and production supplies. Complete cycle counts for raw materials, tooling, and other inventory as assigned. Assist with raw material containment and required inventory or material adjustments. Perform routine maintenance and inspections on Hi-Lo/forklift equipment. Follow all safety procedures and material handling requirements. Participate in Kaizen events and continuous improvement activities. Identify and assist with resolving material handling issues. Complete required training and follow established manufacturing systems and processes. Perform other duties as assigned by the supervisor. Valid forklift certification/license preferred or required based on facility requirements. Experience with inventory control and cycle counting preferred. ERP or production reporting system experience is a plus. Basic computer skills, including Microsoft Word and Excel. Good basic math skills. Strong organizational and attention-to-detail skills. Ability to work quickly while maintaining accuracy. Strong teamwork and accountability. Qualifications Ability to safely operate a Hi-Lo/forklift in a manufacturing environment. Ability to lift and move 50+ pounds repeatedly throughout the day. Ability to follow FIFO, inventory, safety, and material handling procedures. Ability to work in a fast-paced environment. Ability to communicate effectively with Production, Quality, Shipping/Receiving, and PC&L teams. Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing and 5S principles is preferred. Knowledge of ISO 9001 and/or IATF/TS 16949 standards is a plus. Ability to stand, walk, bend, reach, push, pull, and lift throughout the workday. Ability to safely operate a forklift/Hi-Lo for extended periods. Previous stick welding experience preferred. Experience using gas metal arc welding equipment. Ability to follow job-specific work instructions. Ability to inspect completed welds and perform rework as needed. Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship. Ability to work 6:00 AM–4:30 PM, Monday–Thursday. Skills MIG Welding: Ability to perform consistent MIG welds on fabricated components. Weld Inspection: Ability to inspect completed welds and identify areas requiring rework. Stick Welding: Previous stick welding experience preferred. Work Instruction Reading: Ability to follow job-specific welding and production instructions. job.description: Assembly/Machine Operator Location: Newaygo, MI Pay: $18.07/hr Shift: 2nd & 3rd Shift Job Summary Are you a motivated and detail-oriented individual looking for a new opportunity? We're seeking Assembler/Machine Operators to join our team in Newaygo, MI. As part of the Workbox Family, you will receive FREE access to a personalized career consultant, Healthcare Benefits, Disability Insurance, and advancement opportunities. Machine Tending: Proficiency in tending machines to perform force fitting or fastening operations in an assembly cell. Documentation: Ability to complete all necessary paperwork on time and accurately, such as glass traceability, scrap sheets, daily production reports, 5S checklists, and start-up checklists. job.title: Maintenance Technician | 2nd shift | $25+/hr
job.description:
Maintenance Technician
Location: Grandville, MI Shift: 2nd Shift | Flexible Schedule Between 2:00 PM - 12:00 AM (Monday-Friday) Pay: Starting at $25/hr, depending on experience Overtime: May be required as needed
Job Summary
Are you a skilled maintenance professional who enjoys troubleshooting, repairing, and improving industrial equipment? We're seeking a Maintenance Technician to join our team in Grandville, MI. In this hands-on role, you'll perform electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic maintenance on a variety of industrial machinery and equipment while helping ensure safe and efficient plant operations. If you're self- motivated, safety-focused, and thrive working independently, this could be the perfect opportunity for you.
What You'll Be Doing
As a Maintenance Technician, your core responsibilities will include:
? Troubleshooting and repairing equipment: Diagnose and repair electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic systems to minimize downtime.
? Installing and maintaining machinery: Dismantle, assemble, install, and maintain industrial equipment and production machinery.
? Performing electrical work: Troubleshoot and wire 120V, 220V, and 480V circuits, control panels, and related systems.
? Reading technical documentation: Interpret electrical prints, schematics, blueprints, and equipment manuals to facilitate repairs and preventative maintenance activities.
? Performing welding and fabrication: Complete MIG and stick welding repairs on steel up to 1" thick as needed. ? Moving and positioning equipment: Safely rig and move machinery weighing up to 20 tons using lift trucks, overhead cranes, and other rigging equipment. ? Supporting production teams: Assist machine operators in diagnosing equipment malfunctions and implementing corrective actions. ? Maintaining documentation: Accurately document repairs, inspections, and preventative maintenance activities to comply with OSHA, ISO, and company standards.
? Supporting facility maintenance: Assist with general facility upkeep, including HVAC, electrical, plumbing, janitorial services, landscaping, trash removal, parking lot maintenance, and snow removal as needed. ? Promoting workplace safety: Follow company policies and actively support a safe work environment.
What We're Looking For
Qualifications:
? Previous industrial maintenance experience preferred. ? Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
? Strong work ethic and self-motivation. ? Ability to lift up to 100 lbs.
? Willingness to travel up to 20% as needed.
? Comfortable working in a diverse and inclusive team environment. ? Bilingual in English and Spanish preferred.
Skills & Expertise: ? Electrical Maintenance: Experience troubleshooting and repairing industrial electrical systems, including 120V, 220V, and 480V circuits. ? Mechanical Knowledge: Thorough understanding of mechanical systems, industrial machinery, gears, drives, and power transmission equipment.
? Hydraulic & Pneumatic Systems: Ability to diagnose and repair hydraulic and pneumatic components and controls.
? Rigging & Material Handling: Experience moving and positioning heavy equipment using cranes, forklifts, and rigging methods.
? Gear Systems: Working knowledge of large gears, helical gears, and worm drives.
? Welding & Fabrication: Skilled in MIG and stick welding techniques.
? Preventative Maintenance: Experience developing and completing preventative maintenance programs.
? Technical Documentation: Ability to read and interpret blueprints, electrical prints, schematics, and equipment manuals.
Why Join Us?
This opportunity offers a stable career with a company that values technical skills, safety, and continuous improvement. You'll work with a variety of industrial equipment, tackle new challenges daily, and play a critical role in keeping operations running efficiently.

• Weekly Pay • Hire-in Opportunities • Comprehensive Benefits including Health, Life, and Dental Insurance • Veteran-Friendly and Equal Opportunity Employer

job.title: 1st shift - Mechanical Engineer
job.description:
Mechanical Engineer
Location: Grand Rapids, MI Shift: 1st shift Pay: $30/Hour
Are you an experienced mechanical designer with a background in industrial automation? We're seeking a Mechanical Engineer to join our team in Grand Rapids, MI. This position is responsible for the design and development of intelligent systems and industrial automation equipment from initial concept through completion and customer runoff.
What You'll Be DoingAs a Mechanical Engineer, your core responsibilities will include:Project collaboration: Work closely with project managers and customers from the initial design concept through project completion and customer runoff. Design development: Contribute to manufacturing design processes and concepts by collaborating with Estimating, Controls, and Project Management teams. Project ownership: Take ownership of the complete mechanical design life cycle for assigned projects. Fixture design: Apply knowledge of GD&T to develop successful fixturing solutions for assembly applications. Machine design: Design equipment with consideration for machine ergonomics, serviceability, and maintenance. Structural engineering: Engineer structural components and validate designs using FEA. Automation design: Design and develop mechanical systems for industrial automation applications. Customer communication: Communicate effectively with customers, suppliers, and internal team members throughout the project. Project management: Manage multiple tasks and projects simultaneously while maintaining attention to detail. Teamwork: Work collaboratively in a team-based environment and assist with other related duties as needed. Confidentiality: Maintain confidentiality when working with sensitive customer and company projects. Professionalism: Maintain a professional appearance and demeanor at all times. Adaptability: Remain flexible and productive in a fast-paced and frequently changing environment.
What We're Looking For
QualificationsBachelor's degree in Engineering or equivalent relevant industry experience. 10 years of related work experience preferred. Direct experience with mechanical design as a primary responsibility. Strong knowledge and experience with SOLIDWORKS mechanical design software. Understanding of GD&T and mechanical fixturing. Experience with structural engineering and FEA. Strong interpersonal and communication skills. Ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously. Strong attention to detail. Ability to maintain confidentiality on sensitive projects. Ability to work effectively in a team-based environment. Legally authorized to work in the United States without company sponsorship. SkillsMechanical design: Strong understanding of mechanical design principles and industrial automation equipment. SOLIDWORKS: Proficient in using SOLIDWORKS for mechanical design and development. Problem solving: Able to develop practical and effective design solutions for complex manufacturing applications. Communication: Able to communicate clearly and professionally with customers, suppliers, project managers, and team members. Organization: Able to manage multiple projects and priorities while maintaining accuracy and deadlines. Ability to work in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. Ability to effectively manage multiple jobs and projects. Ability to lift up to 40 pounds. Blueprint reading: Able to understand and follow blueprints, engineering sketches, manuals, and specifications. Attention to detail: Able to build and assemble components accurately while maintaining quality standards. job.description:
MIG Welder Location: Fort Wayne, IN Shift: 6:00 AM–4:30 PM | Monday–Thursday Pay: $20.00/hour Job Summary We're looking for a skilled and dependable MIG Welder to join our manufacturing team. This position is responsible for performing manual MIG welding operations, interpreting engineering drawings, and producing high-quality welded products that meet company and customer specifications. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, safety-conscious, and takes pride in delivering quality workmanship. What You'll Be Doing As a MIG Welder, your core responsibilities will include: Performing MIG Welding Operations: Set up component parts in fixtures and perform manual MIG welding according to engineering drawings, specifications, and work instructions. Reading Blueprints and Drawings: Analyze engineering drawings, specifications, work instructions, and quality documents to plan layout, assembly, and welding operations. Inspecting Weld Quality: Examine completed welds and workpieces to ensure products meet quality and performance standards. Using Hand and Power Tools: Safely operate hand tools such as files, hammers, and snips, as well as power tools including sanders, drills, riveters, and grinders. Maintaining Production Standards: Complete work efficiently while meeting production schedules and quality requirements. Following Safety Procedures: Maintain a clean, organized work area and adhere to all company safety policies and procedures. In addition, you may assist with material handling, equipment maintenance, and other fabrication duties as assigned. What We're Looking For Qualifications Previous MIG welding experience preferred. Ability to read and interpret blueprints, engineering drawings, and specifications. Experience using common hand and power tools. Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality. Ability to work independently and as part of a team. Reliable attendance and strong work ethic. Skills MIG Welding: Ability to perform quality welds that meet specifications and standards. Blueprint Reading: Ability to accurately interpret engineering drawings and work instructions. Quality Control: Ability to inspect welds and identify defects or inconsistencies. Tool Operation: Experience using hand tools and fabrication equipment safely and effectively. Problem Solving: Ability to identify issues and make necessary adjustments during fabrication processes. Safety Awareness: Commitment to maintaining a safe and organized work environment. Physical Requirements Ability to stand and work on your feet for extended periods. Ability to lift up to 50 pounds as needed. Ability to bend, reach, twist, and perform repetitive motions throughout the shift. Ability to safely operate welding equipment, hand tools, and power tools. Ability to work in a manufacturing environment with exposure to noise, welding fumes, and production equipment. Why Join Us? Ready for a day in the life of a MIG Welder? This opportunity offers a four-day workweek, competitive pay, and the chance to contribute to a team dedicated to producing high-quality fabricated products. job.title: 1st shift - Pipe Fitter
job.description:
Job Descriptions Job title: Pipe Fitter Reports to: Plant Manager Supervisory responsibilities: n/a Summary/objective: This position is responsible for building and installing pneumatic and water systems on custom tooling and robotic cells. Qualifying candidates will be capable to cut, thread, and hang black pipe or PVC headerson new machinery, run water and air lines to robots and tooling, and assemble pneumatic systems including assembly valve and manifolds banks per Drawings. Essential functions: Manage workload by setting priority of work orders Ensure that all projects are delivered on-time and within scope Configure pipe systems per Engineering Drawings and system layouts Use common equipment and machinery (saws, pipe thread machines, and sometimes cutting torches) to cut, bend and thread pipes to desired specifications Run PVC and black pipe headers for water circuits on custom automated machinery and robotic and cells Ensure that work is done in a consistent manner, meeting all codes and policies in place Light travel for onsite installation of equipment at customer’s facility Follow all company safety protocol Required competency, education, and experience: 2-5 years’ experience and understanding of the automation industry Experience reading and interpreting work instructions and pneumatic blueprints Knowledge and understanding of industry standard components (Parker, SMC, Festo) Knowledge of water cooling circuits for welding systems Ability to apply common sense understanding Ability to carry out written or oral instructions Experience using hand tools, saws, pipe cutting and pipe threading equipment Knowledge and understanding of pilot operated checks (PO Checks) and valve configurations Knowledge and understanding of filter regulators Knowledge of different thread types such as NPT, straight, British and g-thread Knowledge of different valve styles and flow controls Accurate and precise attention to detail while cutting, bending, and installing pipe systems Work environment: Manufacturing environment. Physical demands: Must be able to lift to 50 lbs. on a regular basis Must be able to stand for long periods of time on cement surface and will be required to regularly bend, stretch, stoop, squat, climb ladders and perform work in confined positions. Position type and expected hours of work: Full time. Travel: None Compensation/Benefits: STS offers a competitive compensation and benefits package which includes competitive pay, dental insurance, vision insurance, health insurance, short term disability, long term disability, company paid life insurance, voluntary life insurance, 401(k) plan with match, education reimbursement, paid vacation and holidays, and flex spending. Other duties: This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change, or new ones may be assigned at any time with or without notice. STS is an Equal Opportunity Employer. STS does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, non-disqualifying physical or mental disability, national origin, veteran status, or any other basis covered by appropriate law. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business need. Pipe Fitter
Location: Grand Rapids, MI Shift: 1st shift Pay: $18/Hour
Are you experienced with pipe fitting, pneumatic systems, and custom machinery? We're seeking a Pipe Fitter to join our team in Grand Rapids, MI. This position involves building and installing pneumatic and water systems on custom tooling, automated machinery, and robotic cells.
What You'll Be DoingAs a Pipe Fitter, your core responsibilities will include:Pipe system installation: Build and install pneumatic and water systems on custom tooling, automated machinery, and robotic cells. Pipe fabrication: Cut, bend, thread, and install black pipe and PVC headers according to engineering drawings and system layouts. Pneumatic systems: Assemble pneumatic systems, including valve and manifold banks, according to drawings and specifications. Water & air lines: Run water and air lines to robots, tooling, and other equipment. Engineering drawings: Configure pipe systems according to engineering drawings, work instructions, and system layouts. Equipment operation: Safely operate saws, pipe threading machines, and cutting equipment as required. Workload management: Prioritize work orders and manage workload to keep projects moving efficiently. Project completion: Help ensure projects are completed on time and within the required scope. Quality & compliance: Ensure work is performed consistently and according to applicable codes, company policies, and procedures. Customer installation: Assist with onsite installation of equipment at customer facilities when required. Safety: Follow all company safety protocols and maintain a safe work environment.
What We're Looking ForQualifications2–5 years of experience with an understanding of the automation industry. Experience reading and interpreting work instructions and pneumatic blueprints. Knowledge of industry-standard pneumatic components such as Parker, SMC, and Festo. Knowledge of water cooling circuits used for welding systems. Experience using hand tools, saws, pipe cutting equipment, and pipe threading equipment. Knowledge of pilot-operated checks (PO Checks) and valve configurations. Knowledge of filter regulators. Knowledge of different thread types, including NPT, straight, British, and G-thread. Knowledge of different valve styles and flow controls. Ability to understand and follow written and verbal instructions. Ability to use common-sense understanding when performing job duties. Strong attention to detail and accuracy when cutting, bending, and installing pipe systems. SkillsPipe fitting: Skilled in cutting, bending, threading, and installing pipe systems. Pneumatic systems: Understanding of pneumatic components, valves, manifolds, flow controls, and regulators. Blueprint reading: Able to interpret pneumatic blueprints, engineering drawings, and system layouts. Attention to detail: Precise when measuring, cutting, bending, and installing piping. Problem solving: Able to identify issues with pipe and pneumatic systems and determine appropriate solutions. Organization: Able to prioritize work orders and manage multiple project requirements. Safety: Understands the importance of following safety procedures and applicable codes. Teamwork: Works effectively with team members and other departments to complete projects. job.title: Press Operator
job.description: Press OperatorLocation: Grand Ledge, MI Shift: 5:00 am – 3:30 PM Mon -Thu any OT will be on Friday.Pay: $17.27 Job SummaryWe’re looking for a reliable and detail-oriented Press Operator to join a busy molding and production team. In this role, you will operate presses, mix resin, prepare molds, inspect finished parts, and complete required documentation. The ideal candidate is safety-focused, mechanically inclined, and able to follow detailed production specifications. What You’ll Be DoingPour resin onto fiberglass sheets according to production specification sheets. Track production counts using counters and complete required paperwork. Clean molds using air hoses, apply mold wax, and prepare materials for production. Measure and mix resin and catalyst using dipsticks and air mixers. Operate presses safely and efficiently. Place fiberglass sheets into molds and verify part accuracy using fixtures and measurement tools. Work with robotics to verify water jet accuracy during first-part runs. Inspect parts for defects, perform minor repairs, and complete rework as needed. Adjust mold compression timing and temperature as instructed. Replace empty resin barrels and maintain clean buckets and molds. Conduct first-part runs, complete SPC charts, and obtain supervisor approval. Stamp parts with date and lot numbers. Clean resin run-out, gel coat, and machine beds. Record measurements on ratio logs and calculate mix ratios three times per shift. Report production numbers to supervisors. Troubleshoot production issues as part of a team. Review production boards to determine job numbers, lot numbers, and resin requirements. Spray adhesive and place tags as required. Complete Mix Ratio Logs and perform testing as needed per lab instructions. What We’re Looking ForQualifications:High school diploma or GED required. Ability to follow detailed work instructions and production specifications. Strong attention to detail and mechanical aptitude. Safety-focused and able to work in a fast-paced environment. Prior molding or finishing experience preferred but not required. Skills:Ability to operate presses and related molding equipment. Basic math and measurement skills. Ability to perform minor part repairs and quality checks. Strong teamwork and communication skills. Why Join Us?This is a great opportunity to grow your skills in a hands-on manufacturing environment while working with a team committed to quality, safety, and continuous improvement. job.title: 1st Shift - Forklift/ Material Handler
job.description:
GENERAL SAFETY TRAINING
WORKBOX STAFFING, LLC 1350 Scribner Avenue NW, Grand Rapids, MI 49504 GENERAL SAFETY RULES 2 HAZARD COMMUNICATION – RIGHT TO KNOW 4 EMERGENCY PROCEDURES 10 BLOOD BORNE PATHOGENS 10 PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE) 12 13 EYE PROTECTION 15 HEAD PROTECTION 16 FOOT PROTECTION 17 HEARING PROTECTION 18 HAND PROTECTION 19 MACHINE GUARDING 20 CONFINED SPACE 21 LOCK OUT TAG OUT 21 PREVENTING SLIPS AND FALLS 23 PROPER LIFTING TECHNIQUES
1 GENERAL SAFETY RULES
1. Report to work rested, alert and fit to give your full attention to the job. Of course alcohol and drug use is prohibited on the premises as is the residual results of use. Any employee discovered under the influence of alcohol or drugs will be terminated.
2. All work-related injuries must be reported to your supervisor and Workbox Staffing immediately.
3. Report any unsafe conditions to your supervisor and Workbox Staffing. NO EMPLOYEE IS EVER REQUIRED to perform work that he or she believes is unsafe, or that he or she thinks is likely to cause injury or a health risk to themselves or others. Contact WorkBox immediately if you have any safety concerns your worksite supervisor cannot address.
4. Horseplay, ‘practical jokes,’ etc., are forbidden. Employees are required to work in an injury-free manner displaying accepted levels of behavior. Conduct that places the employee or others at risk, or which threatens or intimidates others, is forbidden.
5. You are responsible to keep your work area clean and safe. Maintain a general condition of good housekeeping in all work areas at all times.
6. Learn where fire extinguishers and first aid kits are located at each assignment.
7. At the time of your work assignment you will be instructed on wearing Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) if it is required for the assignment: Inspect PPE prior to each use. Do not use damaged PPE. You are required to maintain and keep PPE clean. Not wearing required PPE is cause for disciplinary action up to and including termination.
8. You must specifically be authorized by WorkBox and trained by your supervisor to operate the following equipment INCLUDING, but not limited to: Forklifts, Machines, Power Tools, Welders, and Cranes/ Hoist while on assignment. Contact WorkBox immediately if you are asked to do
9. When operating machines: do not wear loose clothing, ensure that long hair is tied- back, remove jewelry, and keep long sleeves either rolled up or pulled all the way down.
10. Never operate damaged or defective equipment. Turn the machine off and report it to your supervisor immediately.
11. Never tamper with, remove, or deactivate machine guards or controls designed to ensure safe operation. Never operate machinery without guards in place.
2 12. Never reach into a machine to clear a jam, clean inside the machine or for any other reason unless it has been properly locked out at the power source(s).
13. Do not remove any lock or tag from machinery. 14. Use proper lifting techniques and if an item is too heavy or awkward to lift, look for
an alternative method and/or have another employee help you lift the item. 15. Learn safe work practices. When in doubt about performing a task safely, contact
your supervisor for instructions and training. 16. Always perform your assigned tasks in a safe and proper manner; do not take
shortcuts. The taking of shortcuts and the ignoring of established safety rules is a leading cause of employee injury.
3 HAZARD COMMUNICATION – RIGHT TO KNOW
If your assignment or work site has or uses any hazardous chemicals you will get specific training on the handling, personal protective equipment required, and use of these chemicals at your job site. This training is a basic introduction to OSHA requirements.
PURPOSE OF OSHA’S HAZARD COMMUNICATION STANDARD
To ensure that employers and employees know about work hazards and how to protect themselves so that the incidence of illnesses and injuries due to hazardous chemicals is reduced.
EMPLOYER RESPONSIBILITIES
• Identify and list hazardous chemicals in their workplaces • Obtain Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) and labels for each hazardous chemical, if not
provided by the manufacturer, importer, or distributor • Implement a written HazCom program, including labels, SDSs, and employee
training • Communicate hazard information to employees through labels, SDSs, and formal
training programs
WRITTEN HAZCOM PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS
• Describes container labeling, SDSs, and employee training for each workplace • List of the hazardous chemicals • Make information regarding hazards and protective measures available to other
employers onsite
HOW MUST CHEMICALS BE LABELED?
Each container of hazardous chemicals entering the workplace must be labeled or marked with:
• Identity of the chemical • Appropriate hazard warnings • Name and address of the responsible party
4 SAMPLES OF LABELING AND HOW TO READ LABELS
Chemical Name 0 = minimal hazard 1 = slight hazard
HEALTH 0 2 = moderate hazard FLAMMABILITY 3 = serious hazard
0 4 = severe hazard
PHYSICAL HAZARD 0
PERSONAL PROTECTION 0 SPECIAL HAZARD
The Blue Section – Health Risks
4 The substance is a severe health risk if the substance is not handled safely. Substances carrying a four in the blue section could cause
death or irreversible injury.
3 The substance could cause serious temporary or irreversible injury. 2 The substance could cause temporary incapacitation. 1 The substance could cause irritation. 0 There is no health hazard.
5 The Red Section – Fire Risks
4 A flammable vapor or gas, which burns readily. 3 A flammable liquid or solid, which can be readily ignited. 2 The substance must be heated for ignition. 1 The substance must be preheated before ignition can occur. 0 There is no fire hazard.
The Yellow Section – Reactivity Hazard
4 The substance is readily capable of detonation or explosive reaction. 3 The substance may detonate when exposed to heat or an ignition
source.
2 The substance is readily capable of non-explosive reaction. 1 The substance may become unstable at high temperatures. 0 The substance is stable.
The White Section – Special Hazards
OX Oxidizer ACID Acid ALK Alkali COR Corrosive
W Use no water
Radioactive
6 PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT
7 Safety Data Sheets (SDS)
The location of SDS Sheets is noted on your employee assignment sheet and/or communicated to by your site supervisor at the start of your assignment. These sheets are prepared by the chemical manufacturer or importer and describe:
• Physical hazards, such as fire and explosion • Health hazards, such as signs of exposure • Routes of exposure • Precautions for safe handling and use • Emergency and first-aid procedures • Control measures • Must be in English and include information regarding the specific chemical identity
and common names • Must provide information about the:
• Physical and chemical characteristics • Health effects • Exposure limits • Carcinogenicity (cancer-causing) • Identification (name, address, and telephone number) of the organization
responsible for preparing the sheet • Must be readily accessible to employees in their work area
EMPLOYEE RESPONSIBILITY - SAFETY HANDLING OF CHEMICALS
a) Do not handle chemicals that you are not trained to handle.
b) A Safety Data Sheet (SDS) must be secured for all chemicals purchased or brought on site. You have a right to access SDSs – ask your supervisor.
c) Follow all label and SDS instructions – including amount instructions
d) Do not mix chemicals unless authorized to do so.
e) Keep all chemicals in closed containers.
8 f) Store all flammable liquids in safety cabinets or safety cans. Never use flammable chemicals around ignition sources such as smokers, pilot lights, or arcing/sparking electrical equipment.
g) Wear required Personal Protective Equipment and minimize contact with the chemical.
h) Do not eat, drink, or smoke while using chemicals. And always wash your hands after handling chemicals.
i) Do not attempt to clean up a hazardous substance unless you are properly trained and authorized.
9 EMERGENCY PROCEDURES
1. In the event of any serious injury or fire, call 911 unless specifically directed or trained by your site supervisor to use a different number or protocol. Send someone to the facility entrance to meet the Fire Department. If in doubt, call 911.
2. Should you discover a fire while on assignment, alert others in immediate danger and initiate facility-wide fire alarm.
3. When an evacuation signal is given for any reason, all employees should immediately turn off equipment, close doors, and evacuate to their designated evacuation areas. Attendance should be taken to account for all personnel. Stay together in the group until further instructions are received.
4. WorkBox does not expect their employees to fight fires at the workplace. Your first priority is your safety and the safety of others. Under no circumstances should you attempt to fight any fire which is larger than a waste basket, too hot, too smoky, or if you are concerned for your safety.
5. If you choose to use a fire extinguisher, remember PASS:
• P = Pull (the safety pin) • A = Aim (at the base of the fire) • S = Squeeze (the lever) • S = Sweep (side to side)
If you use a fire extinguisher, remember:
• Stay low, • Keep yourself between the fire and an exit, • Do not turn your back on a fire, and • Immediately report the use of the extinguisher to your site supervisor and
to your WorkBox supervisor..
BLOOD BORNE PATHOGENS
The term ‘universal precautions’ means that you should assume that blood or other bodily fluids contain bloodborne pathogens that can cause disease and to protect yourself accordingly. Do not touch another person’s blood or any other bodily fluid during or following an incident. If you are trained to administer first aid, use gloves and other barriers that should be located with the first aid equipment. Always use protective personal equipment such as gloves if cleaning up blood or other bodily fluid and use a diluted bleach solution or other sanitizing agent. Dispose of PPE and cleaning towels in a secure way that won’t potentially infect others. If you think that you have been exposed to bodily fluid, notify your site supervisor and your WorkBox supervisor immediately.
10 11 PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE)
PPE includes all equipment designed to provide protection to the wearer from potential hazards to the eyes, face hands, head, feet, ears, and extremities.
Eye/Face Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to the face and eyes during exposure to such hazards as: flying particles, molten metal or sparks, liquid chemicals, acids or caustic liquids, or potentially injurious light radiation (i.e., lasers, welding etc.)
Foot Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to the feet and toes during exposure to situations with the potential for foot injuries such as: falling or rolling objects, chemical or liquid exposures, piercing objects through the sole or uppers, and/or where the employee’s feet are exposed to electrical hazards.
Hand Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to the hands during exposures to potential hazards such as sharp objects, abrasive surfaces, temperature extremes, and chemical contact. Hand protection is selected based upon the hazards and performance characteristics of the gloves.
Head Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to the head during exposures to potential hazards such as falling objects, striking against low hanging objects, or electrical hazards.
Hearing Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to an individual’s hearing during exposure to high noise levels.
Respiratory Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to the wearer from potential inhalation hazards such as: vapors, mist, particulates, and gases.
EMPLOYEE RESPONSIBILITY
1. The employee assignment sheet outlines the basic safety equipment that is required to be worn when on assignment.
2. Additional PPE may be required when performing certain tasks. Your site supervisor is responsible for training you and showing you the proper use and wear of PPE.
3. You are expected to attend the required training.
4. You are also responsible for caring for, cleaning, storing and maintaining PPE as required.
5. Inform your site supervisor immediately of the need to repair or replace PPE. Also inform your WorkBox supervisor.
12 EYE PROTECTION
What are some of the causes of eye injuries?
• Dust and other flying particles, such as metal shavings or sawdust • Molten metal that might splash • Acids and other caustic liquid chemicals that might splash • Blood and other potentially infectious body fluids that might splash, spray, or splatter • Intense light such as those created by welding and lasers
Safety Glasses
• Used for moderate impact from particles produced from jobs such as: carpentry, woodworking, grinding, and machine operation.
• Requires side shields. • Prescription glasses are not safety glasses. You are required
to have other prescription safety glasses.
Goggles
• Used to protect eyes, eye sockets, and the facial area immediately by surrounding the eyes from impact, dust, and splashes.
• Some goggles fit over corrective lenses.
13 EYE PROTECTION (CONTINUED)
Welding Shield
• Protects eyes and burns caused by infrared or intense radiant light.
• Protects face and eyes from flying sparks, metal splatter, and slag chips produced during welding, brazing, soldering, and torch cutting.
Laser Safety Goggles
• Protects your eyes from intense concentration of light produced by lasers.
• Used in conjunction with curtains.
Face Shields
• Protects the face from nuisance dust and potential splashes or sprays of hazardous liquids.
• Does not protect employees from impact hazards. • Safety glasses should be worn underneath shield.
14 HEAD PROTECTION
What are some of the causes of head injuries? • Falling objects • Bumping head against fixed objects, such as exposed pipes or beams • Contact with exposed electrical conductors
Classes of Hard Hats
Class G (formerly Class A) • General service (e.g., mining, building construction, shipbuilding, and manufacturing) • Good impact protection but limited voltage protection
Class E (formerly Class B) • Electrical work • Protect against falling objects, high-voltage shock/burns
Class C • Designed for comfort, offers limited protection • Protects heads that may bump against fixed objects, but does not protect against falling objects or electrical shock
Hard Hats
• Hard hats offer more protection than bump caps. They have an outer shell that is hard and durable to deflect potential head blows. Inside, hard harts have a lining that is shock absorbing. Also, some hard hats can provide protection from electrical shocks.
Bump Hats
• Bump caps are more lightweight than hard hats, making them more comfortable and proving to be less stressful on your neck, head, and back.
• They are ideal in situations where it is not required to wear a hard hat, but injury could still occur. They are often used in warehouses and food processing plants.
15 FOOT PROTECTION
What are some causes of foot injuries?
• Heavy objects such as barrels or tools that might roll onto or fall on the employee’s feet • Sharp objects such as nails or spikes that might pierce the soles or uppers of ordinary
shoes • Molten metal that might splash on feet • Hot or wet surfaces • Slippery surfaces
Steel Toe Shoes/Boots • Safety shoes/boots that have steel reinforced toes in case
something fall on your feet.
• Commonly required by some employers and readily
available at most shoe stores.
Metatarsal Boots and Covers
• Protects the upper foot (metatarsal bones) and toe area from hazards. A work boot with a built-in metatarsal guard will protect your upper foot and toe area from heavy falling objects- especially important for a workspace with heavy equipment, machinery, and containers.
Rubber Sole/Non-slip/Closed Toe Footwear
• You are required to wear rubber sole/non-slip/closed toe footwear on all assignments.
Rubber Boots
• To be used when working in slippery/wet conditions and while using chemicals.
16 HEARING PROTECTION
When do you need hearing protections?
• Noise can damage your hearing permanently whether at work, home, or during leisure activities.
• If the noise is 85 decibels or more, you are required to use ear protection. • A general way to measure this is if you have to raise your voice to talk to the people
standing next to you.
Earplugs
• Reduces noise levels to protect hearing. • These are convenient and disposable.
Earmuffs
• Easy to use and comfortable to wear. • Reduces noise levels to protect hearing.
Canal Caps
• Easy to use and comfortable to wear. • Reduces noise levels to protect hearing. • Hearing protection on a band that can be worn under
the chin, over the head, or behind the neck. • These can be put on and taken off easily.
17 HAND PROTECTION
Common Hand Injuries you need to guard against
• Burns • Bruises • Abrasions • Cuts • Punctures • Fractures • Amputations • Chemical Exposure
Metal Mesh Gloves or Kevlar Gloves
These gloves are used to protect hands from accidental cuts and scratches. They are most commonly used by persons working with cutting tools or other sharp objects and materials.
Fabric/Canvas Gloves
Made of cotton or fabric blends and are generally used to improve grip when handling slippery objects. They also help insulate hands from mild heat or cold. These gloves do not provide a lot of protection against cuts or lacerations.
Leather Gloves
These gloves are used to guard against injuries from sparks or scraping against rough surfaces. They are also used in combination with an insulated liner when working with electricity.
Aluminized Gloves
Gloves made of aluminized fabric are designed to insulate hands from intense heat. These gloves are most commonly when working with molten materials.
Chemical Resistant Gloves
These gloves are made of rubber, neoprene, polyvinyl alcohol, or vinyl. The gloves protect from corrosives, oils, and solvents. You should consult your supervisor for the proper hand protection.
18 MACHINE GUARDING
The machines you work with can contain moving parts with many hazards. Best safety practices involve the use of engineering controls and safe work procedures designed and developed to protect you when working with machines. This includes the use of machine guards. Machine guards safely contain and create a barrier of protection against the dangers.
• Know the potential hazards associated with the machines you use • Understand the role of machine guards and their function • Follow safe work practices when working with machines • Inspect the machine guards on a regular basis • Report any missing or malfunctioning guard immediately
NEVER REMOVE GUARDS
As a machine operator, you are directly affected by machine related hazards. Personal protective equipment, engineering controls, and safe work practices are all important parts of a safe working environment. Machine guards are only one part of this formula.
It is your responsibility to never remove or override these safeguards. A guard that is overridden or disregarded is the same as no guard at all.
EXPOSURE TO ENERGIZED PARTS
Contact with energized parts can cause electrical shock. The severity of the shock is determined by: the nominal voltage, the length of contact, the route of electricity through the body.
EXPOSURE TO MOVING PARTS
Nip points, pinch points, shear points and snag points are the cause of many finger and hand injuries including amputation when not properly respected. Motions such as rotating, reciprocating and transversing, become hazardous when clothing, jewelry or skin contact moving parts. Conveyor belts, gears and couplings are all examples of machine parts with hazardous motions. Actions occur at the point of operation and usually involve one of the three types of motions described earlier. Actions include: Cutting, Punching, Shearing, and Bending.
PROJECTILES
Projectiles from scrap material and foreign objects such as dropped tools can cause injury when working with machines. If an area with parts moving at high speeds is not properly guarded, a tool or item dropped or knocked into this area can become a dangerous projectile.
19 MACHINE GUARDING (Continued)
CATEGORIES OF GUARDS There are a great number of different types of machine guards found in the work environment. All types of machine guards fall into one of three categories: Barrier guards, Distance guards and Physical guards. Fixed
A fixed guard is a permanent fixture of the machine and does not depend on moving parts to function. It is generally constructed of sheet metal, screen, wire cloth, bars, plastic, or any other material that can withstand impacts and prolonged use.
Interlocked
When an interlocked guard is opened or removed, the tripping mechanism and/or power automatically shuts off, effectively stopping all moving parts. This prevents the machine from cycling or starting until the guard is back in place. An interlocked guard uses electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, or pneumatic power or any combination of these.
Adjustable
Adjustable guards provide a barrier that can be adjusted for various production operations.
Self-adjusting
A self-adjusting guard automatically adjusts for the size of the stock. Once the stock is removed, the guard returns to its normal resting position. It may be constructed of plastic, metal, or any other substantial material.
CONFINED SPACE
WorkBox does not allow temporary employees in permit-required confined space. If you believe that your job requires permit-required confined space entry, contact your WorkBox supervisor prior to undertaking the work. (Permit-required confined spaces are areas not meant for human occupancy, have limited means of entry/exit, and have electrical, chemical, thermal, atmosphere, or entrapment hazards).
20 LOCK OUT TAG OUT
Prior to working on any machinery when guards are removed, every energy source (electrical, hydraulic, chemical, mechanical, etc.) must be deactivated, stored energy dissipated, and the control (for example, the circuit breaker) padlocked so the machine cannot be started without removing the lock.
Never remove or tamper with a lockout performed by another employee or contractor. A lockout consists of a lock applied to a control such as a switch, breaker, or valve. A tag containing words such as “DANGER - DO NOT OPERATE” may also be used if the machine cannot be locked out for some reason (‘tagout’). If you see the lock, the tag, or both applied to an energy control device it means, “Keep your hands off.”
If you are asked to clean, clear out a jam or maintain machinery that exposes you to moving or energized parts, you must be trained in the machine-specific lockout procedure and follow that procedure exactly. In no case should you put your hands or body inside a machine that has not been properly locked out at the energy source by you.
PREVENTING SLIPS AND FALLS
You can reduce the risk of slipping by:
1. Taking your time and paying attention to where you are going 2. Adjusting your stride to a pace that is suitable for the walking surface and the task you are
doing 3. Walking with the feet pointing slightly outward 4. Making wide turns at corners 5. Wearing slip resistance shoes 6. Looking out for foreign substances on floors, such as: deposits of water, food, oil, sawdust,
soap, or debris 7. Immediately reporting, cleaning up and/or posting warnings about the presence of water
and other slipping hazards when you see them so others don’t slip.
You can reduce the risk of tripping by:
1. Keeping standing and walking areas clear from clutter or obstructions. Notify a site supervisor if necessary.
2. Keeping flooring in good condition 3. Always using installed light sources that provide sufficient light for your tasks 4. Using a flashlight if you enter a dark room where there is no light 5. Ensuring that things you are carrying or pushing do not prevent you from seeing any
obstructions, spills, etc.
21 Ladders and work at heights: WorkBox has height restrictions for temporary assignments. You should not climb ladders or work at heights that require your feet to be more than xx feet off the ground. 1. Inspect all ladders prior to each use 2. Ladders must be placed on secure footing 3. Only one person is allowed on a ladder at a time 4. Never stand on the top two steps of a stepladder 5. Always maintain 3-point contact when working on ladders 6. Never reach beyond arm length when working on a ladder 7. Never use metal ladders when working on or around electrical equipment or electrical
wires Other work at heights could include lifts or raised work areas. You must be trained by your site supervisor in proper fall protection guidelines and provided with adequate fall protection whenever you are working more than six feet off the ground. Cranes/Hoist/Lifting Devices: 1. Inspect all cranes, hoists, and lifting devices (slings, hooks, etc.) prior to each use, and
never use damaged equipment 2. Never walk under a load suspended from a hoist or crane 3. Keep all personnel clear of the ‘fall zone’ of the crane/hoist 4. Know the weight of material being lifted, and never overload a crane/hoist 5. Do not operate devices unless you have completed the required safety training
22 PROPER LIFTING TECHNIQUES
Plan ahead before lifting. Knowing what you're doing and where you're going will prevent you from making awkward movements while holding something heavy. Clear a path, and if lifting something with another person, make sure both of you agree on the plan.
Lift close to your body. You will be a stronger, and more stable lifter if the object is held close to your body rather than at the end of your reach. Make sure you have a firm hold on the object you are lifting, and keep it balanced close to your body.
Feet shoulder width apart. A solid base of support is important while lifting. Holding your feet too close together will be unstable, too far apart will hinder movement. Keep the feet about shoulder width apart and take short steps.
Bend your knees and keep your back straight. Practice the lifting motion before you lift the object, and think about your motion before you lift. Focus on keeping your spine straight--raise and lower to the ground by bending your knees.
Tighten your stomach muscles. Tightening your abdominal muscles will hold your back in a good lifting position and will help prevent excessive force on the spine.
Lift with your legs. Your legs are many times stronger than your back muscles--let your strength work in your favor. Again, lower to the ground by bending your knees, not your back. Keeping your eyes focused upwards helps to keep your back straight.
If you're straining, get help. If an object is too heavy, or awkward in shape, make sure you have someone around who can help you lift.
Wear a belt or back support. If you are lifting in your job or often at home, a back belt can help you maintain a better lifting posture.
TIPS
Never bend your back to pick something up. It's just not worth the damage that improper lifting technique can cause. Remember to use your leg muscles to help you lift properly.
Hold the object close to your body. You are a much more stable lifter if you're not reaching for an object.
Don't twist or bend. Face in the direction you are walking. If you need to turn, stop, turn in small steps, and then continue walking.
Keep your eyes up. Looking slightly upwards will help you maintain a better position of the spine.

job.description:
Job Title: Press Operator
Division: Burnside Acquisition
Department: 5100
Reports To: Production Supervisor
FLSA Status: Non-Exempt
Prepared Date: 09/09/26
Summary: Safely operate production progressive die, and hand-transfer die, metal stamping equipment to produce the required number of parts that meet customer and company quality standards in a timely manner
Essential Duties and Responsibilities include the following. Other duties may be assigned.
Safely start, run, and shut down an automatic metal stamping press, conveyors, air-blow off devices, feed and straightening equipment.
Skilled in adjusting the press to set and center dies and bring parts into tolerance, experienced with feeding steel from coiler, through straightener, through feeder into the die, know how to adjust roller pressure on said equipment to influence material presentation and control through the die, understand how feed and alignment of material influence part performance. Must be able to use calipers, micrometers, digital indicators, and complex gauges for checking part conformance to tolerances.
Set up all peripheral equipment such as guards, conveyors, and lubricators
Produce the required number of parts the meet customer and quality standards in a timely manner
Perform production related quality tasks such as using hand held gauges to measure or gauging parts, properly handle non-conforming material, properly label and package parts, properly complete the quality documentation system forms and comply with company calibration procedures
Perform operator preventive maintenance on automatic metal stamping press including but not limited to cleaning slugs and scrap from the press bed, press reservoirs, press trays, under and around the press, maintaining coolant and hydraulic oil levels, wiping down workbench surfaces, press control surfaces, monitor motor belts for damage or replacement needs, powering all equipment off when not in use (not leaving it to run while on break or at lunch, or during excessive downtime), proper care of shaker trays and motors.
Safely operate a forklift.
Ensure that housekeeping at the work station is clean, neat and organized while in operation and at the end of shift
Education and/or Experience:
High school diploma or general education degree (GED); or one to three months related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Competencies:
To perform the job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following competencies: Diversity - Demonstrates knowledge of EEO policy; Shows respect and sensitivity for cultural differences; Promotes a harassment-free environment... Ethics - Treats people with respect; Keeps commitments; inspires the trust of others; Works with integrity and ethically; Upholds organizational values. Organizational Support - Follows policies and procedures; Supports organization's goals and values; Supports affirmative action and respects diversity. Planning/Organizing - Uses time efficiently. Quality - Demonstrates accuracy and thoroughness; Looks for ways to improve and promote quality; Applies feedback to improve performance; Monitors own work to ensure quality. Quantity - Meets productivity standards; Completes work in timely manner; Strives to increase productivity; Works quickly. Safety and Security - Observes safety and security procedures; Determines appropriate action beyond guidelines; Reports potentially unsafe conditions; Uses equipment and materials properly. Adaptability - Adapts to changes in the work environment; Manages competing demands; Changes approach or method to best fit the situation; Able to deal with frequent change, delays, or unexpected events. Attendance/Punctuality - Is consistently at work and on time. Dependability - Follows instructions, responds to management direction; Takes responsibility for own actions; Keeps commitments; Commits to long hours of work when necessary to reach goals. Completes tasks on time or notifies appropriate person with an alternate plan.
Language Skills:
Ability to read and comprehend simple instructions, short correspondence, and memos. Ability to write simple correspondence. Ability to effectively present information in one-on-one and small group situations to customers, clients, and other employees of the organization.
Mathematical Skills:
Ability to add, subtracts, multiply, and divides in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals. Ability to compute rate, ratio, and percent and to draw and interpret bar graphs.
Reasoning Ability:
Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out detailed but uninvolved written or oral instructions. Ability to deal with problems involving a few concrete variables in standardized situations. Other Skills and Abilities:
Must be able to speak and write fluent English
Physical Demands:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this Job, the employee is regularly required to stand; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to walk and sit. The employee is occasionally required to climb or balance and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must regularly lift and /or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision and depth perception.
Work Environment:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this Job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts. The noise level in the work environment is usually loud.

job.title: 1st Shift - CNC Operator
job.description:
Job Title: CNC Machinist/Operator Location: American Fabricated Products Company Overview: American Fab is a leading manufacturing company specializing in Prime and Sub-Prime Defense Contractors, Automotive & Furniture OEMs and their sub-tiers as well as many other Industrial markets. We are dedicated to delivering high-quality precision components to our clients while maintaining efficient production processes. As we continue to expand, we are seeking a skilled CNC Operator to join our team and contribute to our success. Position Overview: We are looking for a detail-oriented and experienced CNC Operator to set up, operate, and maintain our computer numerical control (CNC) machines. The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of CNC programming, machining techniques, and a commitment to producing quality products within specified deadlines. The CNC Operator will play a crucial role in ensuring the accuracy and efficiency of our manufacturing processes. Responsibilities: Set up and operate CNC machines according to specifications, blueprints, and job routers. Load raw materials into the machine and secure them properly. Monitor machine operations to ensure quality and adjust machine settings as needed. Interpret CNC programs and make necessary adjustments to optimize production. Conduct routine maintenance on machines to ensure they are in good working condition. Inspect finished products for quality and accuracy, making any necessary adjustments. Troubleshoot issues with machines and perform minor repairs as needed. Adhere to safety protocols and maintain a clean and organized work area. Collaborate with other team members to achieve production goals and meet deadlines. Document production activities and maintain records of machine settings and adjustments. Qualifications: High school diploma or equivalent; technical certification or degree in machining or related field preferred. Proven experience as a CNC Operator or similar role in a manufacturing environment. Strong understanding of CNC programming, machining techniques, and tooling. Proficiency in reading blueprints, schematics, and technical drawings. Ability to use precision measuring tools, such as calipers and micrometers. Excellent attention to detail and problem-solving skills. Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced environment. Strong communication skills and the ability to follow instructions accurately. Knowledge of safety procedures and protocols for operating machinery. Flexibility to work various shifts and overtime as needed. CNC Operator Spring Lake, MI, 1st shift, $22.00 per hour
Job SummaryAre you an experienced CNC Operator looking for an opportunity to grow your skills in a fast-paced manufacturing environment? We’re seeking a dependable and detail-oriented individual to join our team in Spring Lake, MI. In this role, you’ll play a key part in producing high-quality machined parts while ensuring efficiency and accuracy throughout the process.

What We're Looking For Qualifications: High school diploma or equivalent preferred Previous CNC operating experience required Ability to lift up to 50 lbs and stand for extended periods
Skills: Ability to read and interpret blueprints and measurements Strong attention to detail and problem-solving skills Mechanical aptitude and ability to make machine adjustments

job.title: Press Operator - 1st Shift
job.description:
Job Title: Press Operator
Division: Burnside Acquisition
Department: 5100
Reports To: Production Supervisor
FLSA Status: Non-Exempt
Prepared Date: 09/09/26
Summary: Safely operate production progressive die, and hand-transfer die, metal stamping equipment to produce the required number of parts that meet customer and company quality standards in a timely manner
Essential Duties and Responsibilities include the following. Other duties may be assigned.
Safely start, run, and shut down an automatic metal stamping press, conveyors, air-blow off devices, feed and straightening equipment.
Skilled in adjusting the press to set and center dies and bring parts into tolerance, experienced with feeding steel from coiler, through straightener, through feeder into the die, know how to adjust roller pressure on said equipment to influence material presentation and control through the die, understand how feed and alignment of material influence part performance. Must be able to use calipers, micrometers, digital indicators, and complex gauges for checking part conformance to tolerances.
Set up all peripheral equipment such as guards, conveyors, and lubricators
Produce the required number of parts the meet customer and quality standards in a timely manner
Perform production related quality tasks such as using hand held gauges to measure or gauging parts, properly handle non-conforming material, properly label and package parts, properly complete the quality documentation system forms and comply with company calibration procedures
Perform operator preventive maintenance on automatic metal stamping press including but not limited to cleaning slugs and scrap from the press bed, press reservoirs, press trays, under and around the press, maintaining coolant and hydraulic oil levels, wiping down workbench surfaces, press control surfaces, monitor motor belts for damage or replacement needs, powering all equipment off when not in use (not leaving it to run while on break or at lunch, or during excessive downtime), proper care of shaker trays and motors.
Safely operate a forklift.
Ensure that housekeeping at the work station is clean, neat and organized while in operation and at the end of shift
Education and/or Experience:
High school diploma or general education degree (GED); or one to three months related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Competencies:
To perform the job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following competencies: Diversity - Demonstrates knowledge of EEO policy; Shows respect and sensitivity for cultural differences; Promotes a harassment-free environment... Ethics - Treats people with respect; Keeps commitments; inspires the trust of others; Works with integrity and ethically; Upholds organizational values. Organizational Support - Follows policies and procedures; Supports organization's goals and values; Supports affirmative action and respects diversity. Planning/Organizing - Uses time efficiently. Quality - Demonstrates accuracy and thoroughness; Looks for ways to improve and promote quality; Applies feedback to improve performance; Monitors own work to ensure quality. Quantity - Meets productivity standards; Completes work in timely manner; Strives to increase productivity; Works quickly. Safety and Security - Observes safety and security procedures; Determines appropriate action beyond guidelines; Reports potentially unsafe conditions; Uses equipment and materials properly. Adaptability - Adapts to changes in the work environment; Manages competing demands; Changes approach or method to best fit the situation; Able to deal with frequent change, delays, or unexpected events. Attendance/Punctuality - Is consistently at work and on time. Dependability - Follows instructions, responds to management direction; Takes responsibility for own actions; Keeps commitments; Commits to long hours of work when necessary to reach goals. Completes tasks on time or notifies appropriate person with an alternate plan.
Language Skills:
Ability to read and comprehend simple instructions, short correspondence, and memos. Ability to write simple correspondence. Ability to effectively present information in one-on-one and small group situations to customers, clients, and other employees of the organization.
Mathematical Skills:
Ability to add, subtracts, multiply, and divides in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals. Ability to compute rate, ratio, and percent and to draw and interpret bar graphs.
Reasoning Ability:
Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out detailed but uninvolved written or oral instructions. Ability to deal with problems involving a few concrete variables in standardized situations. Other Skills and Abilities:
Must be able to speak and write fluent English
Physical Demands:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this Job, the employee is regularly required to stand; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to walk and sit. The employee is occasionally required to climb or balance and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must regularly lift and /or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision and depth perception.
Work Environment:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this Job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts. The noise level in the work environment is usually loud.
The employer reserves the right to revise this job description at any time. Responsibilities may vary. Issue Date: ____________________________ Revised date: 9/09/26 I agree to, and understand the responsibilities listed above. I accept the duties of this position.
