job.description: Lead Operator Location: Grand Rapids, MI Shift: 1st shift 6:00 am – 3:30 pm 2nd Shift 4:30 pm -2:00 am Pay: $20.00 //$ 22.00 per hour Job Summary The Lead Operator is the bridge between the production assembly track and the supervisory track. It is the first leadership tier on the floor. The Lead Operator performs hands-on production work as the primary part of the role while also leading their line, setting the example for quality and pace, helping others, and keeping the line running. The Lead Operator works without a supervisor present as needed, executing the work order on hand and resolving minor issues on their own line. This is a working leadership role, not a desk role. What You'll Be Doing As a Lead Operator, your core responsibilities will include: Production Perform hands-on production work as the primary part of the role. Lead the assigned line and set the standard for quality, safety, and pace. Cover absent operators on the line as needed. Perform routine equipment setup and changeover. Work without a supervisor present as needed, executing the work order on hand within the scope of the line. Directing and Assigning Assign tasks and workstations to employees on the line. Direct the work of the line, typically 5 to 12 employees. Execute the schedule and priorities set by the supervisor; escalate when changes are needed rather than redirecting independently. Problem Solving Resolve minor production problems on the line without escalation, with primary judgment over parts shortages and material handler coordination. Escalate quality stoppages and safety work stoppages immediately to the supervisor; the Lead Operators do not hold independent stop authority at this tier. Report employee conduct issues with the shift supervisor. People and Training Show others proper technique on the job (informal, on-the-line instruction). Serve as an operator a new hire can shadow, where in good standing. Provide verbal shift handoff to the Area Lead or Shift Lead. In addition, you will also be expected to monitor and maintain the output for the assigned line as well as maintaining a safe and organized workflow. What We're Looking For To be successful in this role, you should have the following: Qualifications: Previous experience in production assembly lines of 2 or more years Experience in a team lead, supervisory, or manager role of 1 or more years Ability to lift, bend, twist, stoop, and maneuver 50 lbs. throughout a full 8-hour shift Skills: Expert knowledge of the products and processes on the assigned line. Sound independent judgment within the scope of the line. Clear verbal communication, up and across the line. Ownership of the line's output; reliable and present. Advanced assembly knowledge, tool proficiency, and the ability to troubleshoot common line issues. Why Join Us? This is an excellent opportunity for both short-term and long-term employment. We are committed to providing a supportive work environment and opportunities for growth. job.title: 1st Shift - Delivery Helper
job.description:
Delivery Helper – 1st Shift Location: Zeeland, MI Shift: 1st Shift | 6:30 AM–4:00/5:00 PM Pay: $20.00/hour Job Summary We're looking for a dependable and hardworking Delivery Helper to join our team in Zeeland, MI. In this hands-on role, you'll ride along with a delivery driver and assist with loading, unloading, carrying, and placing sheets of drywall and other construction-related materials at customer job sites. This is a physically demanding position that requires frequent heavy lifting, working outdoors in varying weather conditions, and providing professional service at customer locations. The ideal candidate is safety-focused, dependable, and comfortable with a fast-paced, physical workday. What You'll Be Doing As a Delivery Helper, your core responsibilities will include: Drywall Loading & Unloading: Load and unload sheets of drywall and other construction materials from delivery vehicles. Material Carrying & Placement: Safely carry construction materials from the truck and place them in designated areas at customer job sites. Delivery Assistance: Ride along with the delivery driver and assist with locating job sites, organizing deliveries, and completing assigned routes efficiently. Job Site Support: Help prepare delivery areas before unloading and restore job sites after deliveries are completed. Product Handling: Carefully handle drywall and other construction materials to prevent damage to products and customer property. Load Securement: Help properly secure drywall, construction materials, equipment, metal, pallets, and other products on the truck. Pre-Trip Preparation: Assist with inspections of equipment, paperwork, and loaded products to ensure orders are accurate and ready for delivery. Truck & Equipment Care: Help maintain delivery equipment and prepare materials and equipment for the following day's deliveries. Warehouse Support: Assist with staging, organizing, loading, and other warehouse responsibilities between deliveries as needed. Safety Compliance: Follow company procedures and applicable OSHA and DOT safety guidelines while loading, transporting, and unloading materials. In addition, you'll communicate professionally with customers and coworkers while helping ensure deliveries are completed safely, accurately, and on schedule. What We're Looking For Qualifications Previous delivery, construction, warehouse, material handling, or general labor experience preferred. Must be comfortable loading, unloading, and carrying sheets of drywall and other construction-related materials. Ability to read, write, follow directions, and communicate information accurately. Ability to lift at least 75 pounds and frequently move materials weighing up to 100 pounds. Ability to safely load and unload materials from flatbed or boom trucks. Comfortable performing repetitive, physically demanding work throughout the shift. Must be comfortable working outdoors in varying weather conditions. Ability to follow company, OSHA, and DOT safety procedures. Ability to work independently and as part of a delivery team. Strong attendance, dependability, and initiative. Flexibility to work until approximately 4:00–5:00 PM, depending on delivery routes and daily workload. Skills Drywall & Construction Material Handling: Ability to safely lift, carry, load, unload, and place drywall and other construction materials. Heavy Material Handling: Ability to safely maneuver large, bulky, and heavy materials while preventing damage. Delivery Support: Ability to work alongside the driver to ensure materials are delivered safely, accurately, and efficiently. Customer Service: Professional and courteous communication when working at customer locations. Communication: Ability to accurately receive instructions and quickly communicate problems or concerns. Organization & Prioritization: Ability to manage multiple deliveries, job sites, and customer deadlines. Teamwork: Ability to work closely with the driver and other team members when handling large or heavy materials. Safety Awareness: Strong commitment to proper lifting, material handling, load securement, and job site safety procedures. Physical Requirements Ability to remain standing and physically active for approximately 90% of the workday. Ability to lift at least 75 pounds and frequently move materials weighing up to 100 pounds. Ability to repeatedly lift and carry sheets of drywall and other bulky construction materials throughout the shift. job.description:
MIG Welder Location: Holland, MI Shift: 1st Shift | 6:00 AM–2:00 PM | Monday–Friday Pay: $22.00–$24.00/hour Job Summary Are you an experienced welder who takes pride in producing strong, high-quality work? We're looking for a skilled MIG Welder to join our manufacturing team in Holland, MI. In this role, you'll perform MIG welding on outdoor patio tables and chairs, helping fabricate and assemble quality finished products. The ideal candidate has previous MIG welding experience, is comfortable working in a metal fabrication environment, and takes pride in producing clean, consistent welds. What You'll Be Doing As a MIG Welder, your core responsibilities will include: MIG Welding: Perform MIG welding on components used to manufacture outdoor patio tables and chairs. Product Assembly: Fit, position, and weld components together to produce completed patio furniture. Steel Fabrication: Assist with the fabrication and assembly of steel components used throughout the manufacturing process. Fit-Up: Properly position and align parts prior to welding to ensure accurate assembly. Quality Inspection: Inspect completed welds and fabricated components to ensure they meet quality standards. Production Support: Work alongside the fabrication team to keep products moving efficiently through production. Safety & Housekeeping: Maintain a clean and organized work area while following all company safety procedures. In addition, you'll work in a manufacturing environment specializing in steel fabrication, laser cutting, tube and wire bending, and welding. What We're Looking For Qualifications Previous MIG welding experience required. Previous steel fabrication or metalworking experience preferred. Ability to fit and align components prior to welding. Ability to work safely in a manufacturing and fabrication environment. Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship. Reliable attendance and strong work ethic. Ability to work independently and as part of a team. Skills MIG Welding: Ability to produce consistent, quality MIG welds on steel components. Fabrication & Assembly: Ability to fit, position, weld, and assemble components used to manufacture outdoor patio furniture. Mechanical Aptitude: Comfortable working with fabricated metal components and welding equipment. Quality Focus: Ability to inspect completed welds and identify potential quality concerns. Attention to Detail: Ability to maintain accuracy and consistency throughout the welding process. Teamwork: Ability to work effectively with welders, fabricators, and other production team members. Safety Awareness: Commitment to following proper welding and manufacturing safety procedures. Why Join Us? This 1st Shift MIG Welder opportunity offers $22.00–$24.00/hour with consistent 6:00 AM–2:00 PM, Monday–Friday hours. It's a great opportunity for an experienced MIG Welder looking for hands-on fabrication work producing outdoor patio tables and chairs. job.description: Administrative Assistant Location: Grand Rapids, MI Shift: 1st Shift Pay: $18.00+ per hour Based on experience Job SummaryOur team is seeking a highly organized, reliable, and detail-oriented Office Administrator to manage daily office operations and provide essential support across financial, administrative, and sales functions within a fast-paced manufacturing environment. The ideal candidate is a self-starter with excellent communication skills who can work independently and as part of a team to ensure smooth business operations. Collaborate closely with team members in a manufacturing environment to support business operations and customer needs. Complete assignments independently with a high degree of accuracy, reliability, and timeliness. Utilize extensive hands-on experience with QuickBooks Platinum to support accounting, reporting, and operational activities. job.title: 2nd Shift - Material Handler / Logistics Associate
job.description: Material Handler / Logistics Associate Location: New Boston, MI Shift: 1st Shift Pay: $18/hr Job Summary Are you an experienced forklift operator who enjoys variety in your workday? We’re seeking dependable Material Handlers / Logistics Associates to join a fast-paced warehouse team in New Boston, MI. This temp-to-hire opportunity is ideal for someone who thrives in a dynamic environment, is willing to jump in where needed, and enjoys a mix of forklift operation and hands-on warehouse work. What You’ll Be Doing As a Logistics Associate, your core responsibilities will include: Forklift Operation: Safely operate both sit-down and stand-up forklifts to move, stack, stage, and transport materials throughout the facility. Material Handling & Shipping Support: Assist with re-pack and banding stations to secure products for shipment and support overall warehouse operations. Warehouse Team Support: Maintain a “wherever needed” mindset by rotating between forklift duties and manual warehouse tasks to support the Logistics Team and daily production needs. In addition, you will maintain inventory accuracy during material movement, follow all safety procedures, assist with staging materials, and support efficient warehouse flow in a fast-paced environment. What We’re Looking For To be successful in this role, you should have the following: Qualifications: Minimum 6 months of provable forklift experience within the last 18 months required. Experience operating either sit-down OR stand-up forklifts required. Must be willing to learn and use both types of forklifts. Ability and willingness to perform manual labor, including banding, re-packing, and material handling tasks. Must be flexible and willing to work mandatory overtime, including arriving early, staying late, or working weekends as needed. Strong attendance, reliability, and work ethic required. Skills: Forklift Proficiency: Safe and efficient operation of warehouse equipment. Flexibility: Ability to shift between equipment operation and hands-on labor tasks as needed. Safety Awareness: Commitment to following safety protocols and maintaining an organized workspace. Teamwork: Strong communication skills and willingness to support team goals. Why Join Us? This is an excellent opportunity for both short-term and long-term employment with the opportunity for permanent hire after 480 hours. We are committed to providing a supportive work environment and opportunities for growth. job.description:
JOB TITLE DEPARTMENT CREATED
Quality Engineer Quality 02/21/24
POSITION DESCRIPTION
Support position with primary activities being the development and management of facility Advanced Product Quality Planning and PPAP process.
PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
Develop and implement the customer and internal requirements of process manuals and quality standards f.or takeover tooling, including updates/changes resulting from engineering changes. Work closely with the Quality Technician in the development of the decision making documents to be used i.n the manufacturing process. Lead the development process of the Process FMEA’s. Initiate customer or internal, sample submission activities for transfer tool program. Manage Product drawings from receipt to file location/current revision. Coordinate the development of information supporting sample submission activities, such as: G. age R&R studies; Dimensional Layout(s); Capability Studies; Laboratory Material Testing; Performance Testing; Fit and function. Obtain and verify compliance of submitted documentation of internal process/inspection plans, measurement results and capability studies.
ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES
Maintain and apply Corrective Action process, as required. Offer support and guidance as needed to the Quality Technician to manage and administer measurement .equipment calibration activities as required. Manage annual customer product revalidations as required. Obtain and verify submission documentation from suppliers, as required. Support customer requirements - customer visits. Assist in development, organization, and maintenance of the quality reporting system. This includes, but is not limited to the following: Internal scrap to include ppm reporting activities and associated top contributor b. readksowns on an effective basis; Customer product rejections to include daily ppm reporting activities and a. ssocated top contributor breakdowns on an effective basis. Coordinate the development of information supporting production part approval submission activities, such as: D. imensional layouts; Capability studies. OTHER REQUIREMENTS
Associates degree from a college or university or a minimum of two years quality engineering experience or a. n equivalent combination of education and experience. Proficient in personal computer use and network operation. Ability to read, interpret documents, communicated effectively across all levels, and present information t.o various group. Ability at math, percentages, proportions, and basic statistics. Ability to manage problem-solving activities. Ability to apply logic to follow written, oral, or diagram instructions. Completion of training requirements matrix.
POSITION KEY INTERFACES
INTERNAL EXTERNAL
All Clarion’s associates at a single location Customers Clarion Corporate program support Suppliers

Teamwork/interpersonal skills Judgement/Decision making Attention to detail and accuracy of work Communication Skills

Quality Engineer
Location: Greenville, MI Pay: 60k-75k depending on experience Shift: 1st shift
Job Summary The Quality Engineer is responsible for supporting the development and management of the facility’s Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) and Production Part Approval Process (PPAP). This position works closely with Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, suppliers, and customers to ensure quality requirements are met throughout the product and tooling process.
Essential Duties & Responsibilities Develop and implement customer and internal requirements for process manuals and quality standards related to takeover tooling. Maintain and update quality documentation as engineering changes occur. Work closely with the Quality Technician to develop decision-making documents used in the manufacturing process. Lead the development of Process Failure Mode and Effects Analyses (PFMEAs). Initiate and coordinate customer and internal sample submission activities for transfer tooling programs. Manage product drawings from receipt through proper filing and revision control. Coordinate documentation and activities supporting sample submissions, including:Gage R&R studies Dimensional layouts Capability studies Laboratory material testing Performance testing Fit and function testing Obtain and verify internal process and inspection plans, measurement results, capability studies, and other required documentation. Maintain and apply the corrective action process as needed. Support and provide guidance to the Quality Technician with measurement equipment calibration activities. Manage annual customer product revalidations. Obtain and verify required quality documentation from suppliers. Support customer requirements and customer visits. Assist with the development, organization, and maintenance of the quality reporting system. Monitor and report internal scrap, including PPM reporting and analysis of top contributors. Monitor and report customer product rejections, including daily PPM reporting and analysis of top contributors. Coordinate the development of information required for production part approval submissions, including dimensional layouts and capability studies. Qualifications & Requirements Associate degree from a college or university or a minimum of two years of Quality Engineering experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Proficient in personal computer use and network operations. Ability to read and interpret documents and communicate effectively with employees at all levels. Ability to present information to various groups. Strong understanding of mathematics, percentages, proportions, and basic statistics. Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills. Ability to apply logic and follow written, verbal, and diagram instructions. Strong attention to detail and accuracy. Good teamwork and interpersonal skills. Ability to complete required training programs. Key Skills APQP & PPAP PFMEA Corrective Action Quality Documentation Capability Studies Gage R&R Dimensional Layouts Quality Reporting Problem Solving Data Analysis Communication & Teamwork Why Join Us? This is an excellent opportunity for both short-term and long-term employment. We’re committed to providing a supportive work environment, opportunities for growth, and a team that cares.Workbox Staffing Benefits

job.title: Machine Operator III
job.description: Machine Operator III – 3rd Shift Location: Holland, MI Shift: 3rd Shift | 8:30 PM–7:00 AM | Sunday–Thursday Pay: $19.00–$21.00/hour Job Summary We're looking for an experienced and mechanically inclined Machine Operator III to join our 3rd Shift production team in Holland, MI. In this role, you'll set up, adjust, and safely operate a variety of machines used to cut and slot partitions from different types of roll stock according to specifications. This position requires strong machine setup and troubleshooting skills, attention to product quality, and the ability to recognize and correct operating issues independently. What You'll Be Doing As a Machine Operator III, your core responsibilities will include: Machine Setup & Operation: Set up, adjust, and safely operate machines used to cut and slot partitions according to production specifications. Equipment Adjustments: Work from patterns to mount and adjust dies, guides, feeds, speeds, tension, and other machine settings. Troubleshooting: Recognize operating problems and make necessary adjustments for stock variations, worn dies, humidity, and other production conditions. Quality Control: Take responsibility for product quality and use board gauges, rules, patterns, and other inspection tools to verify specifications. Material Handling: Move and change rolls, transport strip loads and scrap loads, and safely operate hand and power trucks. Machine Maintenance: Perform routine machine repairs, lubrication, and preventive maintenance as needed. Production Documentation: Accurately record and report production times, materials produced, equipment problems, and other required information. Production Scheduling: Work from manufacturing requirement schedules to complete assigned production work efficiently. Training & Cross-Training: Train other team members, answer questions regarding stacking and packing procedures, and participate in cross-training. Parts & Supplies: Maintain a working knowledge of material and inventory identification and requisition parts and supplies as needed. Safety: Practice and promote safe work habits while immediately reporting unsafe conditions or equipment requiring repair. In addition, you'll maintain expected productivity levels, communicate effectively with team members and leadership, and help create a positive, team-based production environment. What We're Looking For Qualifications Previous machine operation experience required. Strong experience with machine setup and adjustments. Ability to independently complete machine setups and work preparation, seeking assistance when unusual circumstances arise. Ability to recognize machine operating problems and make appropriate adjustments. Working knowledge of materials and inventory identification. Ability to safely operate machines, hand tools, and powered material-handling equipment. Ability to perform routine preventive maintenance and basic machine repairs. Ability to follow manufacturing schedules and production specifications. Willingness to participate in cross-training and train other team members. Ability to work effectively in a team-based manufacturing environment. Skills Machine Setup: Ability to mount and adjust dies, guides, feeds, speeds, tension, and other machine settings. Mechanical Troubleshooting: Ability to identify equipment and production problems and make appropriate adjustments. Quality Control: Ability to use board gauges, rules, patterns, and other inspection equipment to maintain product quality. Problem-Solving: Strong ability to recognize production issues and determine appropriate solutions. Preventive Maintenance: Ability to perform routine equipment maintenance, lubrication, and minor repairs. Production Documentation: Ability to accurately record production, material usage, and equipment issues. Training & Leadership: Ability to train team members and provide guidance on production procedures. Communication & Teamwork: Ability to communicate effectively and contribute to a team-based work environment. Safety Awareness: Commitment to practicing and promoting safe work procedures. Why Join Us? This 3rd Shift Machine Operator III opportunity offers $19.00–$21.00/hour with a Sunday–Thursday, 8:30 PM–7:00 AM schedule. This is a great fit for an experienced machine operator who enjoys taking ownership of equipment setup, troubleshooting, quality, and production. job.title: Production Opportunities (Marketing)
job.description:
Production Opportunities Location: Clare, MI Pay: $18.50/hr depending on position/shift Shift: All Shifts Job Summary Are you a motivated and detail-oriented individual looking for a new opportunity? We're seeking a Production Operator to join our team in Clare, MI. In this role, you'll be a vital part of our operations, helping us to ensure quality production through robotic welding and CNC machine operation. What You'll Be Doing As a Production Operator, your core responsibilities will include: Inspecting Incoming Material: Ensuring quality specifications and quantities are met. Operating an Overhead Crane: Receiving and issuing raw material to and from saws, trucks, and storage areas. Robotic Welding and CNC Machine Operation: Programming, setting up, operating, and adjusting process variables to meet quality demands. In addition, you will also be expected to maintain inventory control, complete entry of work orders and packing slips, and perform daily shift maintenance inspections. Not only will you be responsible for inspecting and managing raw materials and operating an overhead crane, but you’ll also be primarily focused on robotic welding and operating other CNC machines, including programming, setup, and adjustment to ensure quality products. What We're Looking For To be successful in this role, you should have the following: Qualifications:High school diploma or equivalent desired. Two years of experience and/or educational related courses on related machinery desired. Experience/knowledge of blueprint reading, AutoCAD, CNC programming, thermal cutting machinery, and welding knowledge preferred. Ability to obtain a Crane License and fork truck license. Ability to read, analyze, and interpret the English language. Satisfactory math skills including addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and basic geometry. Excellent problem-solving abilities. Ability to multi-task. Ability to operate machinery on a three-dimensional basis. Agility of the upper and lower body extremities, and capable of lifting 50 pounds regularly. Skills:Quality Inspection: To inspect incoming material for quality specification and quantities. Material Handling: To receive and issue raw material to and from saws, trucks, and storage areas by operation of an overhead crane. Robotic Welding and CNC Operation: Primary focus would be working on the robotic welder and fabrication of products utilizing other CNC machines, including programming, machine setup, operation, and adjustment of process variables to meet quality demands. Inventory Control: To maintain inventory control by identifying and labeling raw material with proper identification. Computer System Entry: To complete entry of work orders, packing slips, etc., into the main computer system. Welding Knowledge: Must be knowledgeable in welding. Work Order Processing: To receive and issue raw material according to the work order, prints, routings, and bill of lading. Program Selection: To select appropriate programs utilizing the operating software, based upon the work order and print. Verification: Cross-checking that revision, part number, and description are correct. Before loading material into the machine, verify correct amount, size, gauge, and length of material has been loaded into the machine and issued to the work order. Measurement: Utilizing calipers, micrometers, and other measuring devices to verify accuracy. Quality Assurance: To check the quality of the first part for appearance and that the part meets print specifications. Assures that the fit, function, and appearance of products are at, or exceed quality standards. Production Fulfillment: Fulfills production requirements. Part Placement: To place finished parts in proper container/rack and designated location. Record Keeping: To record on work order all labor and downtime, documenting all information pertaining to each work order and routing. Maintenance: Performs daily shift maintenance inspection per the preventative maintenance (PM) checklist. Collaboration: Confers with the Team Leader or Crew Leader on any problems regarding safety, quality, production, inventory issues, etc. Confers with Engineering Programmer to maximize potential efficiency and quality gains in the manufacturing process. Work Area Maintenance: Maintain high quality standards as regards to machine and work area. Removal of all metal scrap, debris, and residue from machine as needed. Why Join Us? This is an excellent opportunity for both short-term and long-term employment. We are committed to providing a supportive work environment and opportunities for growth.

job.title: 2nd Shift - Injection Mold Setter
job.description:
2nd Shift - Injection Mold Setter Location: Elkhart, IN Shift: 2nd Shift – M-Th: 1:00pm-10:00pm, F: 1:00pm-5:00pm Pay: Starting at $22.00 per hour, with higher wages available based on experience, technical skill level, and injection molding expertise. Job Summary Are you a mechanically inclined individual looking to grow your career in plastics manufacturing? We're seeking an Injection Molding Setup Technician to join our team in Elkhart, IN. In this role, you'll play a vital part in keeping production running efficiently by performing mold changeovers, troubleshooting equipment, and ensuring injection molding machines consistently produce high-quality parts. If you enjoy working with machinery, solving mechanical problems, and learning new technical skills, we encourage you to apply. What You'll Be Doing As an Injection Molding Setter, your core responsibilities will include: Machine Setup & Changeovers: Install molds and inserts, perform mold and tool changeovers according to production schedules, and prepare machines for efficient production runs. Equipment Maintenance & Troubleshooting: Monitor machine performance, respond to alarms, troubleshoot equipment and part defects, perform preventative maintenance, and maintain dryers, grinders, hoppers, filters, and other support equipment. Material Preparation & Production Support: Prepare and mix raw materials, safely transport molds and materials using a forklift, maintain proper tooling and equipment organization, communicate with production and Quality teams, and support daily production goals while following all company safety and quality standards. In addition, you will also be expected to identify equipment concerns, report maintenance needs, maintain a clean and organized work area, and assist with continuous improvement initiatives. What We're Looking For To be successful in this role, you should have the following: Qualifications: -Previous experience in injection molding or plastics manufacturing preferred
-Experience performing mold changes, machine setups, and equipment troubleshooting -Must be mechanically inclined with a strong interest in working on manufacturing equipment
-Candidates with excellent mechanical aptitude are strongly encouraged to apply
-Forklift operation is required for this position. Previous forklift experience is preferred, but employer-provided training and certification are available for qualified candidates.
-Ability to follow production schedules and work instructions
-Strong communication and teamwork skills
-Ability to lift up to 50 lbs as needed
-Reliable attendance and a strong work ethic
Skills: Mechanical Aptitude: Strong understanding of mechanical systems with the ability to troubleshoot equipment and quickly learn new machinery. Injection Molding Expertise: Knowledge of injection molding machines, mold setup, and production support is preferred. Material Handling: Ability to safely operate a forklift and move molds, raw materials, and finished products throughout the facility. Forklift certification will be provided by the employer. Attention to Detail: Strong focus on quality, process consistency, and maintaining accurate production standards. Why Join Us? This is an excellent opportunity to build a long-term career in a growing manufacturing environment. We offer competitive starting pay with opportunities for increased compensation based on experience, technical ability, and performance. If you're mechanically inclined and enjoy working with machinery, this is an excellent opportunity to develop specialized skills in injection molding while building a rewarding manufacturing career. You'll also receive employer-paid forklift training and certification, allowing you to expand your skill set while working in a hands-on technical role. job.title: 1st Shift - Quality Technician
job.description: Quality Technician Location: Mishawaka, IN Shift: 6:00 AM–2:30 PM | Monday–Friday Pay: $21.00/hour Job Summary We're looking for a detail-oriented Quality Technician to join our manufacturing team. This position is responsible for supporting quality assurance processes through inspections, gauge calibration, data collection, and continuous improvement initiatives. The ideal candidate has experience reading blueprints, understands quality systems, and is committed to ensuring products meet customer and company quality standards. What You'll Be Doing As a Quality Technician, your core responsibilities will include: Calibrating Inspection Equipment: Perform monthly gauge calibrations and maintain accurate calibration records to ensure all equipment remains compliant. Supporting Quality Assurance: Document customer and company quality expectations while participating in daily quality activities. Conducting Continuous Improvement Activities: Participate in capability studies, document corrective actions, and support ongoing quality improvement initiatives. Analyzing Returned Materials: Evaluate returned products, document findings, and assist with corrective action reporting. Maintaining SPC Data: Enter Statistical Process Control (SPC) data into the system and generate reports as needed. Performing Product Inspections: Complete quality inspections, including first-piece and last-piece inspections, while supporting company quality management systems. In addition, you will assist with QS initiatives and perform other quality-related duties as assigned. What We're Looking For Qualifications Previous quality technician or quality inspection experience preferred. Ability to read and interpret blueprints. Knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T). Ability to collect, analyze, and compile quality data into meaningful reports. Understanding of quality standards and manufacturing processes. Reliable attendance and strong work ethic. Skills Blueprint Reading: Ability to accurately interpret engineering drawings and specifications. Quality Systems: Knowledge of quality inspection procedures, gauge calibration, and quality documentation. Data Analysis: Ability to analyze quality data and prepare meaningful reports. Continuous Improvement: Experience supporting corrective actions, capability studies, and process improvements. Computer Skills: Ability to enter and maintain SPC and quality data accurately. Communication & Teamwork: Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate across departments. Physical Requirements Ability to stand and walk for extended periods throughout the shift. Ability to lift up to 50 pounds as needed. Ability to bend, reach, twist, and perform repetitive motions throughout the workday. Ability to perform detailed inspections using measuring equipment. Ability to work in a manufacturing environment while maintaining a clean and organized work area. Why Join Us? Ready for a day in the life of a Quality Technician? This opportunity offers steady first-shift hours, competitive pay, and the chance to play an important role in maintaining product quality while supporting continuous improvement efforts in a team-oriented manufacturing environment. job.description: Production Opportunities Location: Clare, MI Pay: $18.50/hr Shift: All Shifts Job Summary Are you a motivated and detail-oriented individual looking for a new opportunity? We're seeking a Production Operator to join our team in Clare, MI. In this role, you'll be a vital part of our operations, helping us to ensure quality production through robotic welding and CNC machine operation. What You'll Be Doing As a Production Operator, your core responsibilities will include: Inspecting Incoming Material: Ensuring quality specifications and quantities are met. Operating an Overhead Crane: Receiving and issuing raw material to and from saws, trucks, and storage areas. Robotic Welding and CNC Machine Operation: Programming, setting up, operating, and adjusting process variables to meet quality demands. In addition, you will also be expected to maintain inventory control, complete entry of work orders and packing slips, and perform daily shift maintenance inspections. Not only will you be responsible for inspecting and managing raw materials and operating an overhead crane, but you’ll also be primarily focused on robotic welding and operating other CNC machines, including programming, setup, and adjustment to ensure quality products. What We're Looking For To be successful in this role, you should have the following: Qualifications: High school diploma or equivalent desired. Two years of experience and/or educational related courses on related machinery desired. Experience/knowledge of blueprint reading, AutoCAD, CNC programming, thermal cutting machinery, and welding knowledge preferred. Ability to obtain a Crane License and fork truck license. Ability to read, analyze, and interpret the English language. Satisfactory math skills including addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and basic geometry. Excellent problem-solving abilities. Ability to multi-task. Ability to operate machinery on a three-dimensional basis. Agility of the upper and lower body extremities, and capable of lifting 50 pounds regularly. Skills: Quality Inspection: To inspect incoming material for quality specification and quantities. Material Handling: To receive and issue raw material to and from saws, trucks, and storage areas by operation of an overhead crane. Robotic Welding and CNC Operation: Primary focus would be working on the robotic welder and fabrication of products utilizing other CNC machines, including programming, machine setup, operation, and adjustment of process variables to meet quality demands. Inventory Control: To maintain inventory control by identifying and labeling raw material with proper identification. Computer System Entry: To complete entry of work orders, packing slips, etc., into the main computer system. Welding Knowledge: Must be knowledgeable in welding. Work Order Processing: To receive and issue raw material according to the work order, prints, routings, and bill of lading. Program Selection: To select appropriate programs utilizing the operating software, based upon the work order and print. Verification: Cross-checking that revision, part number, and description are correct. Before loading material into the machine, verify correct amount, size, gauge, and length of material has been loaded into the machine and issued to the work order. Measurement: Utilizing calipers, micrometers, and other measuring devices to verify accuracy. Quality Assurance: To check the quality of the first part for appearance and that the part meets print specifications. Assures that the fit, function, and appearance of products are at, or exceed quality standards. Production Fulfillment: Fulfills production requirements. Part Placement: To place finished parts in proper container/rack and designated location. Record Keeping: To record on work order all labor and downtime, documenting all information pertaining to each work order and routing. Maintenance: Performs daily shift maintenance inspection per the preventative maintenance (PM) checklist. Collaboration: Confers with the Team Leader or Crew Leader on any problems regarding safety, quality, production, inventory issues, etc. Confers with Engineering Programmer to maximize potential efficiency and quality gains in the manufacturing process. Work Area Maintenance: Maintain high quality standards as regards to machine and work area. Removal of all metal scrap, debris, and residue from machine as needed. Why Join Us? job.title: CNC Machinist - 1st Shift
job.description:
CNC Machinist Location: Elkhart, IN Shift: 1st Shift | Monday–Friday Pay: $25.00–$37.00/hour Job Summary We're looking for a skilled and experienced CNC Machinist to join a team specializing in the production of custom tooling and fixtures. This position is responsible for setting up, and operating CNC mills and lathes to manufacture precision tooling and fixtures that meet engineering specifications and customer requirements. The ideal candidate has strong blueprint reading skills, 3-5+ years of experience, and takes pride in producing high-quality, precision-machined components. What You'll Be Doing As a CNC Machinist, your core responsibilities will include: Operating CNC Machines: Set up, and operate CNC mills and lathes to manufacture custom tooling and fixtures. Reading Blueprints and Technical Drawings: Interpret blueprints, engineering drawings, and work orders to ensure accurate machining and production. Inspecting Finished Parts: Use precision measuring tools to verify finished tooling and fixtures meet dimensional tolerances and quality standards. Making Machine Adjustments: Monitor machine performance, make tooling changes, and adjust machine offsets to maintain production accuracy. Maintaining Equipment: Perform routine machine maintenance and keep workstations clean, organized, and production-ready. Following Safety Procedures: Adhere to all company safety policies while maintaining a safe and efficient work environment. In addition, you will troubleshoot machining issues, document production information, and collaborate with engineering and production teams to manufacture high-quality custom tooling solutions. What We're Looking For Qualifications Previous CNC machining experience required. 3-5+ Years of Experience programming, setting up, and operating CNC mills and lathes. Blueprint reading experience is required. Experience using precision measuring tools such as calipers, micrometers, indicators, and gauges. Strong mechanical aptitude and troubleshooting skills. Reliable attendance and strong work ethic. Skills Precision Machining: Experience producing custom tooling, fixtures, and precision-machined components. Blueprint Reading: Ability to accurately interpret engineering drawings and machining specifications. Quality Inspection: Skilled in using precision measuring instruments to verify finished parts. Problem Solving: Ability to troubleshoot machining issues and make necessary machine adjustments. Safety Awareness: Commitment to following workplace safety standards and maintaining a clean work environment. Physical Requirements Ability to stand and walk for extended periods throughout the shift. Ability to lift up to 50 pounds as needed. Ability to bend, reach, twist, and perform repetitive motions throughout the workday. Ability to safely operate CNC machinery and precision measuring equipment. Ability to work in a manufacturing environment with exposure to machinery, noise, and metalworking fluids. Why Join Us? Ready for a day in the life of a CNC Machinist? This opportunity offers competitive pay, steady first-shift hours, and the chance to build custom tooling and fixtures using advanced CNC equipment. If you enjoy precision machining and producing one-of-a-kind components, this is an excellent opportunity to grow your career in a highly skilled manufacturing environment. job.title: 2nd Shift - Chemical Blender/ Mixer
job.description:
Chemical Blender / Compounder
Location: Wayne, Michigan Shift: 2nd Pay: Up to $21/hr
Job Summary
Are you an experienced chemical blender looking for an opportunity to work in a fast-paced manufacturing environment? We are seeking a dependable and detail-oriented Chemical Blender / Compounder responsible for setting up mixing tanks and blending equipment to support production operations. This role requires safely handling raw materials, following batch instructions, operating production equipment, and maintaining quality standards while contributing to continuous process improvements.
What You'll Be Doing
As a Chemical Blender / Compounder, your core responsibilities will include:
• Setting up and operating mixing tanks and blending machines according to batch work orders and mixing instructions.
• Supporting production lines by preparing blended materials in a timely and safe manner.
• Filling drums with blended products as needed. • Operating mixers, scales, meters, pumps, forklifts, and other
production equipment safely and efficiently. • Measuring and handling raw materials according to batch
specifications. • Communicating with material handlers to ensure proper material flow
and availability. • Sampling raw materials and preparing documentation for laboratory
testing, including Certificates of Analysis and Safety Data Sheets (SDS). • Providing recommendations to the Blending Manager regarding process improvements and operational efficiencies.
• Ensuring all safety policies and procedures are followed throughout the facility.
• Working independently while maintaining a positive team-oriented attitude.
• Setting up and starting all mixing tanks and blenders. • Supporting production lines to maintain efficient workflow. • Reviewing and understanding all batch documentation to ensure
correct ingredients are used. • Accurately adding chemicals and powders into blend tanks and
ribbon blenders according to established formulas. • Monitoring raw material usage and verifying correct weights and
quantities. • Ensuring returned raw materials are properly labeled, documented,
and stored. • Following laboratory instructions regarding sample logging, batch
approvals, adjustments, and additional quality requirements.
What We're Looking For
Qualifications:
• High school diploma or equivalent work experience. • Previous experience mixing and blending chemicals. • Highly dependable with a strong work ethic. • Ability to think through minor problems and work with management to
resolve larger issues. • Ability to read, comprehend, and follow written and verbal instructions
in English. • Ability to understand safety procedures, operating instructions,
product recipes, and material identification requirements. • Ability to safely manipulate and handle 55-gallon drums of chemicals. • Strong mathematical skills, including addition, subtraction,
multiplication, and division using weight and volume measurements. • Valid forklift certification and ability to safely operate a forklift. • Strong attention to detail and mechanical aptitude.
Skills & Abilities:
• Ability to work independently with minimal supervision. • Strong organizational and time-management skills. • Effective communication skills. • Commitment to workplace safety and quality standards. • Ability to identify opportunities for process improvements.
Equipment Experience:
• Mixing tanks • Ribbon blenders • Industrial mixers • Scales • Meters • Pumps • Forklifts • Drum handling equipment
Physical Requirements:
• Ability to lift, move, and manipulate chemical containers and 55- gallon drums.
• Ability to stand, walk, bend, and perform repetitive tasks throughout the shift.
• Ability to work in a manufacturing environment while following all PPE and safety requirements.
Why Join Us?
This role offers the opportunity to work in a growing manufacturing environment where safety, quality, and teamwork are valued. You'll play a critical role in supporting production operations while helping improve processes and maintain product quality. Workbox Staffing Benefits:
• Weekly Pay • Hire-in Opportunities • Health, Life, and Dental Benefits • Veteran-Friendly and Equal Opportunity Employer Ready to get started? Apply today and let's go to work!

job.title: 1st Shift (Turn 2) - Production Associate (Eastern)
job.description:
GENERAL SAFETY TRAINING
WORKBOX STAFFING, LLC 1350 Scribner Avenue NW, Grand Rapids, MI 49504 GENERAL SAFETY RULES 2 HAZARD COMMUNICATION – RIGHT TO KNOW 4 EMERGENCY PROCEDURES 10 BLOOD BORNE PATHOGENS 10 PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE) 12 13 EYE PROTECTION 15 HEAD PROTECTION 16 FOOT PROTECTION 17 HEARING PROTECTION 18 HAND PROTECTION 19 MACHINE GUARDING 20 CONFINED SPACE 21 LOCK OUT TAG OUT 21 PREVENTING SLIPS AND FALLS 23 PROPER LIFTING TECHNIQUES
1 GENERAL SAFETY RULES
1. Report to work rested, alert and fit to give your full attention to the job. Of course alcohol and drug use is prohibited on the premises as is the residual results of use. Any employee discovered under the influence of alcohol or drugs will be terminated.
2. All work-related injuries must be reported to your supervisor and Workbox Staffing immediately.
3. Report any unsafe conditions to your supervisor and Workbox Staffing. NO EMPLOYEE IS EVER REQUIRED to perform work that he or she believes is unsafe, or that he or she thinks is likely to cause injury or a health risk to themselves or others. Contact WorkBox immediately if you have any safety concerns your worksite supervisor cannot address.
4. Horseplay, ‘practical jokes,’ etc., are forbidden. Employees are required to work in an injury-free manner displaying accepted levels of behavior. Conduct that places the employee or others at risk, or which threatens or intimidates others, is forbidden.
5. You are responsible to keep your work area clean and safe. Maintain a general condition of good housekeeping in all work areas at all times.
6. Learn where fire extinguishers and first aid kits are located at each assignment.
7. At the time of your work assignment you will be instructed on wearing Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) if it is required for the assignment: Inspect PPE prior to each use. Do not use damaged PPE. You are required to maintain and keep PPE clean. Not wearing required PPE is cause for disciplinary action up to and including termination.
8. You must specifically be authorized by WorkBox and trained by your supervisor to operate the following equipment INCLUDING, but not limited to: Forklifts, Machines, Power Tools, Welders, and Cranes/ Hoist while on assignment. Contact WorkBox immediately if you are asked to do
9. When operating machines: do not wear loose clothing, ensure that long hair is tied- back, remove jewelry, and keep long sleeves either rolled up or pulled all the way down.
10. Never operate damaged or defective equipment. Turn the machine off and report it to your supervisor immediately.
11. Never tamper with, remove, or deactivate machine guards or controls designed to ensure safe operation. Never operate machinery without guards in place.
2 12. Never reach into a machine to clear a jam, clean inside the machine or for any other reason unless it has been properly locked out at the power source(s).
13. Do not remove any lock or tag from machinery. 14. Use proper lifting techniques and if an item is too heavy or awkward to lift, look for
an alternative method and/or have another employee help you lift the item. 15. Learn safe work practices. When in doubt about performing a task safely, contact
your supervisor for instructions and training. 16. Always perform your assigned tasks in a safe and proper manner; do not take
shortcuts. The taking of shortcuts and the ignoring of established safety rules is a leading cause of employee injury.
3 HAZARD COMMUNICATION – RIGHT TO KNOW
If your assignment or work site has or uses any hazardous chemicals you will get specific training on the handling, personal protective equipment required, and use of these chemicals at your job site. This training is a basic introduction to OSHA requirements.
PURPOSE OF OSHA’S HAZARD COMMUNICATION STANDARD
To ensure that employers and employees know about work hazards and how to protect themselves so that the incidence of illnesses and injuries due to hazardous chemicals is reduced.
EMPLOYER RESPONSIBILITIES
• Identify and list hazardous chemicals in their workplaces • Obtain Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) and labels for each hazardous chemical, if not
provided by the manufacturer, importer, or distributor • Implement a written HazCom program, including labels, SDSs, and employee
training • Communicate hazard information to employees through labels, SDSs, and formal
training programs
WRITTEN HAZCOM PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS
• Describes container labeling, SDSs, and employee training for each workplace • List of the hazardous chemicals • Make information regarding hazards and protective measures available to other
employers onsite
HOW MUST CHEMICALS BE LABELED?
Each container of hazardous chemicals entering the workplace must be labeled or marked with:
• Identity of the chemical • Appropriate hazard warnings • Name and address of the responsible party
4 SAMPLES OF LABELING AND HOW TO READ LABELS
Chemical Name 0 = minimal hazard 1 = slight hazard
HEALTH 0 2 = moderate hazard FLAMMABILITY 3 = serious hazard
0 4 = severe hazard
PHYSICAL HAZARD 0
PERSONAL PROTECTION 0 SPECIAL HAZARD
The Blue Section – Health Risks
4 The substance is a severe health risk if the substance is not handled safely. Substances carrying a four in the blue section could cause
death or irreversible injury.
3 The substance could cause serious temporary or irreversible injury. 2 The substance could cause temporary incapacitation. 1 The substance could cause irritation. 0 There is no health hazard.
5 The Red Section – Fire Risks
4 A flammable vapor or gas, which burns readily. 3 A flammable liquid or solid, which can be readily ignited. 2 The substance must be heated for ignition. 1 The substance must be preheated before ignition can occur. 0 There is no fire hazard.
The Yellow Section – Reactivity Hazard
4 The substance is readily capable of detonation or explosive reaction. 3 The substance may detonate when exposed to heat or an ignition
source.
2 The substance is readily capable of non-explosive reaction. 1 The substance may become unstable at high temperatures. 0 The substance is stable.
The White Section – Special Hazards
OX Oxidizer ACID Acid ALK Alkali COR Corrosive
W Use no water
Radioactive
6 PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT
7 Safety Data Sheets (SDS)
The location of SDS Sheets is noted on your employee assignment sheet and/or communicated to by your site supervisor at the start of your assignment. These sheets are prepared by the chemical manufacturer or importer and describe:
• Physical hazards, such as fire and explosion • Health hazards, such as signs of exposure • Routes of exposure • Precautions for safe handling and use • Emergency and first-aid procedures • Control measures • Must be in English and include information regarding the specific chemical identity
and common names • Must provide information about the:
• Physical and chemical characteristics • Health effects • Exposure limits • Carcinogenicity (cancer-causing) • Identification (name, address, and telephone number) of the organization
responsible for preparing the sheet • Must be readily accessible to employees in their work area
EMPLOYEE RESPONSIBILITY - SAFETY HANDLING OF CHEMICALS
a) Do not handle chemicals that you are not trained to handle.
b) A Safety Data Sheet (SDS) must be secured for all chemicals purchased or brought on site. You have a right to access SDSs – ask your supervisor.
c) Follow all label and SDS instructions – including amount instructions
d) Do not mix chemicals unless authorized to do so.
e) Keep all chemicals in closed containers.
8 f) Store all flammable liquids in safety cabinets or safety cans. Never use flammable chemicals around ignition sources such as smokers, pilot lights, or arcing/sparking electrical equipment.
g) Wear required Personal Protective Equipment and minimize contact with the chemical.
h) Do not eat, drink, or smoke while using chemicals. And always wash your hands after handling chemicals.
i) Do not attempt to clean up a hazardous substance unless you are properly trained and authorized.
9 EMERGENCY PROCEDURES
1. In the event of any serious injury or fire, call 911 unless specifically directed or trained by your site supervisor to use a different number or protocol. Send someone to the facility entrance to meet the Fire Department. If in doubt, call 911.
2. Should you discover a fire while on assignment, alert others in immediate danger and initiate facility-wide fire alarm.
3. When an evacuation signal is given for any reason, all employees should immediately turn off equipment, close doors, and evacuate to their designated evacuation areas. Attendance should be taken to account for all personnel. Stay together in the group until further instructions are received.
4. WorkBox does not expect their employees to fight fires at the workplace. Your first priority is your safety and the safety of others. Under no circumstances should you attempt to fight any fire which is larger than a waste basket, too hot, too smoky, or if you are concerned for your safety.
5. If you choose to use a fire extinguisher, remember PASS:
• P = Pull (the safety pin) • A = Aim (at the base of the fire) • S = Squeeze (the lever) • S = Sweep (side to side)
If you use a fire extinguisher, remember:
• Stay low, • Keep yourself between the fire and an exit, • Do not turn your back on a fire, and • Immediately report the use of the extinguisher to your site supervisor and
to your WorkBox supervisor..
BLOOD BORNE PATHOGENS
The term ‘universal precautions’ means that you should assume that blood or other bodily fluids contain bloodborne pathogens that can cause disease and to protect yourself accordingly. Do not touch another person’s blood or any other bodily fluid during or following an incident. If you are trained to administer first aid, use gloves and other barriers that should be located with the first aid equipment. Always use protective personal equipment such as gloves if cleaning up blood or other bodily fluid and use a diluted bleach solution or other sanitizing agent. Dispose of PPE and cleaning towels in a secure way that won’t potentially infect others. If you think that you have been exposed to bodily fluid, notify your site supervisor and your WorkBox supervisor immediately.
10 11 PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE)
PPE includes all equipment designed to provide protection to the wearer from potential hazards to the eyes, face hands, head, feet, ears, and extremities.
Eye/Face Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to the face and eyes during exposure to such hazards as: flying particles, molten metal or sparks, liquid chemicals, acids or caustic liquids, or potentially injurious light radiation (i.e., lasers, welding etc.)
Foot Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to the feet and toes during exposure to situations with the potential for foot injuries such as: falling or rolling objects, chemical or liquid exposures, piercing objects through the sole or uppers, and/or where the employee’s feet are exposed to electrical hazards.
Hand Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to the hands during exposures to potential hazards such as sharp objects, abrasive surfaces, temperature extremes, and chemical contact. Hand protection is selected based upon the hazards and performance characteristics of the gloves.
Head Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to the head during exposures to potential hazards such as falling objects, striking against low hanging objects, or electrical hazards.
Hearing Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to an individual’s hearing during exposure to high noise levels.
Respiratory Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to the wearer from potential inhalation hazards such as: vapors, mist, particulates, and gases.
EMPLOYEE RESPONSIBILITY
1. The employee assignment sheet outlines the basic safety equipment that is required to be worn when on assignment.
2. Additional PPE may be required when performing certain tasks. Your site supervisor is responsible for training you and showing you the proper use and wear of PPE.
3. You are expected to attend the required training.
4. You are also responsible for caring for, cleaning, storing and maintaining PPE as required.
5. Inform your site supervisor immediately of the need to repair or replace PPE. Also inform your WorkBox supervisor.
12 EYE PROTECTION
What are some of the causes of eye injuries?
• Dust and other flying particles, such as metal shavings or sawdust • Molten metal that might splash • Acids and other caustic liquid chemicals that might splash • Blood and other potentially infectious body fluids that might splash, spray, or splatter • Intense light such as those created by welding and lasers
Safety Glasses
• Used for moderate impact from particles produced from jobs such as: carpentry, woodworking, grinding, and machine operation.
• Requires side shields. • Prescription glasses are not safety glasses. You are required
to have other prescription safety glasses.
Goggles
• Used to protect eyes, eye sockets, and the facial area immediately by surrounding the eyes from impact, dust, and splashes.
• Some goggles fit over corrective lenses.
13 EYE PROTECTION (CONTINUED)
Welding Shield
• Protects eyes and burns caused by infrared or intense radiant light.
• Protects face and eyes from flying sparks, metal splatter, and slag chips produced during welding, brazing, soldering, and torch cutting.
Laser Safety Goggles
• Protects your eyes from intense concentration of light produced by lasers.
• Used in conjunction with curtains.
Face Shields
• Protects the face from nuisance dust and potential splashes or sprays of hazardous liquids.
• Does not protect employees from impact hazards. • Safety glasses should be worn underneath shield.
14 HEAD PROTECTION
What are some of the causes of head injuries? • Falling objects • Bumping head against fixed objects, such as exposed pipes or beams • Contact with exposed electrical conductors
Classes of Hard Hats
Class G (formerly Class A) • General service (e.g., mining, building construction, shipbuilding, and manufacturing) • Good impact protection but limited voltage protection
Class E (formerly Class B) • Electrical work • Protect against falling objects, high-voltage shock/burns
Class C • Designed for comfort, offers limited protection • Protects heads that may bump against fixed objects, but does not protect against falling objects or electrical shock
Hard Hats
• Hard hats offer more protection than bump caps. They have an outer shell that is hard and durable to deflect potential head blows. Inside, hard harts have a lining that is shock absorbing. Also, some hard hats can provide protection from electrical shocks.
Bump Hats
• Bump caps are more lightweight than hard hats, making them more comfortable and proving to be less stressful on your neck, head, and back.
• They are ideal in situations where it is not required to wear a hard hat, but injury could still occur. They are often used in warehouses and food processing plants.
15 FOOT PROTECTION
What are some causes of foot injuries?
• Heavy objects such as barrels or tools that might roll onto or fall on the employee’s feet • Sharp objects such as nails or spikes that might pierce the soles or uppers of ordinary
shoes • Molten metal that might splash on feet • Hot or wet surfaces • Slippery surfaces
Steel Toe Shoes/Boots • Safety shoes/boots that have steel reinforced toes in case
something fall on your feet.
• Commonly required by some employers and readily
available at most shoe stores.
Metatarsal Boots and Covers
• Protects the upper foot (metatarsal bones) and toe area from hazards. A work boot with a built-in metatarsal guard will protect your upper foot and toe area from heavy falling objects- especially important for a workspace with heavy equipment, machinery, and containers.
Rubber Sole/Non-slip/Closed Toe Footwear
• You are required to wear rubber sole/non-slip/closed toe footwear on all assignments.
Rubber Boots
• To be used when working in slippery/wet conditions and while using chemicals.
16 HEARING PROTECTION
When do you need hearing protections?
• Noise can damage your hearing permanently whether at work, home, or during leisure activities.
• If the noise is 85 decibels or more, you are required to use ear protection. • A general way to measure this is if you have to raise your voice to talk to the people
standing next to you.
Earplugs
• Reduces noise levels to protect hearing. • These are convenient and disposable.
Earmuffs
• Easy to use and comfortable to wear. • Reduces noise levels to protect hearing.
Canal Caps
• Easy to use and comfortable to wear. • Reduces noise levels to protect hearing. • Hearing protection on a band that can be worn under
the chin, over the head, or behind the neck. • These can be put on and taken off easily.
17 HAND PROTECTION
Common Hand Injuries you need to guard against
• Burns • Bruises • Abrasions • Cuts • Punctures • Fractures • Amputations • Chemical Exposure
Metal Mesh Gloves or Kevlar Gloves
These gloves are used to protect hands from accidental cuts and scratches. They are most commonly used by persons working with cutting tools or other sharp objects and materials.
Fabric/Canvas Gloves
Made of cotton or fabric blends and are generally used to improve grip when handling slippery objects. They also help insulate hands from mild heat or cold. These gloves do not provide a lot of protection against cuts or lacerations.
Leather Gloves
These gloves are used to guard against injuries from sparks or scraping against rough surfaces. They are also used in combination with an insulated liner when working with electricity.
Aluminized Gloves
Gloves made of aluminized fabric are designed to insulate hands from intense heat. These gloves are most commonly when working with molten materials.
Chemical Resistant Gloves
These gloves are made of rubber, neoprene, polyvinyl alcohol, or vinyl. The gloves protect from corrosives, oils, and solvents. You should consult your supervisor for the proper hand protection.
18 MACHINE GUARDING
The machines you work with can contain moving parts with many hazards. Best safety practices involve the use of engineering controls and safe work procedures designed and developed to protect you when working with machines. This includes the use of machine guards. Machine guards safely contain and create a barrier of protection against the dangers.
• Know the potential hazards associated with the machines you use • Understand the role of machine guards and their function • Follow safe work practices when working with machines • Inspect the machine guards on a regular basis • Report any missing or malfunctioning guard immediately
NEVER REMOVE GUARDS
As a machine operator, you are directly affected by machine related hazards. Personal protective equipment, engineering controls, and safe work practices are all important parts of a safe working environment. Machine guards are only one part of this formula.
It is your responsibility to never remove or override these safeguards. A guard that is overridden or disregarded is the same as no guard at all.
EXPOSURE TO ENERGIZED PARTS
Contact with energized parts can cause electrical shock. The severity of the shock is determined by: the nominal voltage, the length of contact, the route of electricity through the body.
EXPOSURE TO MOVING PARTS
Nip points, pinch points, shear points and snag points are the cause of many finger and hand injuries including amputation when not properly respected. Motions such as rotating, reciprocating and transversing, become hazardous when clothing, jewelry or skin contact moving parts. Conveyor belts, gears and couplings are all examples of machine parts with hazardous motions. Actions occur at the point of operation and usually involve one of the three types of motions described earlier. Actions include: Cutting, Punching, Shearing, and Bending.
PROJECTILES
Projectiles from scrap material and foreign objects such as dropped tools can cause injury when working with machines. If an area with parts moving at high speeds is not properly guarded, a tool or item dropped or knocked into this area can become a dangerous projectile.
19 MACHINE GUARDING (Continued)
CATEGORIES OF GUARDS There are a great number of different types of machine guards found in the work environment. All types of machine guards fall into one of three categories: Barrier guards, Distance guards and Physical guards. Fixed
A fixed guard is a permanent fixture of the machine and does not depend on moving parts to function. It is generally constructed of sheet metal, screen, wire cloth, bars, plastic, or any other material that can withstand impacts and prolonged use.
Interlocked
When an interlocked guard is opened or removed, the tripping mechanism and/or power automatically shuts off, effectively stopping all moving parts. This prevents the machine from cycling or starting until the guard is back in place. An interlocked guard uses electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, or pneumatic power or any combination of these.
Adjustable
Adjustable guards provide a barrier that can be adjusted for various production operations.
Self-adjusting
A self-adjusting guard automatically adjusts for the size of the stock. Once the stock is removed, the guard returns to its normal resting position. It may be constructed of plastic, metal, or any other substantial material.
CONFINED SPACE
WorkBox does not allow temporary employees in permit-required confined space. If you believe that your job requires permit-required confined space entry, contact your WorkBox supervisor prior to undertaking the work. (Permit-required confined spaces are areas not meant for human occupancy, have limited means of entry/exit, and have electrical, chemical, thermal, atmosphere, or entrapment hazards).
20 LOCK OUT TAG OUT
Prior to working on any machinery when guards are removed, every energy source (electrical, hydraulic, chemical, mechanical, etc.) must be deactivated, stored energy dissipated, and the control (for example, the circuit breaker) padlocked so the machine cannot be started without removing the lock.
Never remove or tamper with a lockout performed by another employee or contractor. A lockout consists of a lock applied to a control such as a switch, breaker, or valve. A tag containing words such as “DANGER - DO NOT OPERATE” may also be used if the machine cannot be locked out for some reason (‘tagout’). If you see the lock, the tag, or both applied to an energy control device it means, “Keep your hands off.”
If you are asked to clean, clear out a jam or maintain machinery that exposes you to moving or energized parts, you must be trained in the machine-specific lockout procedure and follow that procedure exactly. In no case should you put your hands or body inside a machine that has not been properly locked out at the energy source by you.
PREVENTING SLIPS AND FALLS
You can reduce the risk of slipping by:
1. Taking your time and paying attention to where you are going 2. Adjusting your stride to a pace that is suitable for the walking surface and the task you are
doing 3. Walking with the feet pointing slightly outward 4. Making wide turns at corners 5. Wearing slip resistance shoes 6. Looking out for foreign substances on floors, such as: deposits of water, food, oil, sawdust,
soap, or debris 7. Immediately reporting, cleaning up and/or posting warnings about the presence of water
and other slipping hazards when you see them so others don’t slip.
You can reduce the risk of tripping by:
1. Keeping standing and walking areas clear from clutter or obstructions. Notify a site supervisor if necessary.
2. Keeping flooring in good condition 3. Always using installed light sources that provide sufficient light for your tasks 4. Using a flashlight if you enter a dark room where there is no light 5. Ensuring that things you are carrying or pushing do not prevent you from seeing any
obstructions, spills, etc.
21 Ladders and work at heights: WorkBox has height restrictions for temporary assignments. You should not climb ladders or work at heights that require your feet to be more than xx feet off the ground. 1. Inspect all ladders prior to each use 2. Ladders must be placed on secure footing 3. Only one person is allowed on a ladder at a time 4. Never stand on the top two steps of a stepladder 5. Always maintain 3-point contact when working on ladders 6. Never reach beyond arm length when working on a ladder 7. Never use metal ladders when working on or around electrical equipment or electrical
wires Other work at heights could include lifts or raised work areas. You must be trained by your site supervisor in proper fall protection guidelines and provided with adequate fall protection whenever you are working more than six feet off the ground. Cranes/Hoist/Lifting Devices: 1. Inspect all cranes, hoists, and lifting devices (slings, hooks, etc.) prior to each use, and
never use damaged equipment 2. Never walk under a load suspended from a hoist or crane 3. Keep all personnel clear of the ‘fall zone’ of the crane/hoist 4. Know the weight of material being lifted, and never overload a crane/hoist 5. Do not operate devices unless you have completed the required safety training
22 PROPER LIFTING TECHNIQUES
Plan ahead before lifting. Knowing what you're doing and where you're going will prevent you from making awkward movements while holding something heavy. Clear a path, and if lifting something with another person, make sure both of you agree on the plan.
Lift close to your body. You will be a stronger, and more stable lifter if the object is held close to your body rather than at the end of your reach. Make sure you have a firm hold on the object you are lifting, and keep it balanced close to your body.
Feet shoulder width apart. A solid base of support is important while lifting. Holding your feet too close together will be unstable, too far apart will hinder movement. Keep the feet about shoulder width apart and take short steps.
Bend your knees and keep your back straight. Practice the lifting motion before you lift the object, and think about your motion before you lift. Focus on keeping your spine straight--raise and lower to the ground by bending your knees.
Tighten your stomach muscles. Tightening your abdominal muscles will hold your back in a good lifting position and will help prevent excessive force on the spine.
Lift with your legs. Your legs are many times stronger than your back muscles--let your strength work in your favor. Again, lower to the ground by bending your knees, not your back. Keeping your eyes focused upwards helps to keep your back straight.
If you're straining, get help. If an object is too heavy, or awkward in shape, make sure you have someone around who can help you lift.
Wear a belt or back support. If you are lifting in your job or often at home, a back belt can help you maintain a better lifting posture.
TIPS
Never bend your back to pick something up. It's just not worth the damage that improper lifting technique can cause. Remember to use your leg muscles to help you lift properly.
Hold the object close to your body. You are a much more stable lifter if you're not reaching for an object.
Don't twist or bend. Face in the direction you are walking. If you need to turn, stop, turn in small steps, and then continue walking.
Keep your eyes up. Looking slightly upwards will help you maintain a better position of the spine.
23

job.title: Bilingual Recruiter
job.description: Entry Level Job Recruiter - Paid Training Provided! Come Join Us! Workbox Staffing is an industrial staffing firm specializing in the manufacturing and warehousing jobs. We are based in Grand Rapids, Michigan, and have branches in the Midwest, Mid-Atlantic, and Southeast regions of the U.S. market. We strive to make a positive difference in the lives of our employee associates, clients, and teammates. We offer a very competitive starting hourly pay rate with a full benefits package, a 401K plan, paid time off, and promotional opportunities from within. Workbox Staffing is seeking an Entry Level Recruiter to support and grow our community by connecting talented job seekers to local employers. You are an advocate for job seekers and help to provide pathways to employment. You will thrive filling job positions using a full-cycle recruiting method, from talent sourcing and attracting candidates, pre-employment screenings, interviewing, and completion of all onboarding documentation. job.description:
JOB TITLE DEPARTMENT CREATED
Maintenance Technician Technical 7/24/23
POSITION DESCRIPTION
Support position with responsibilities focused upon troubleshooting and repairing electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, or mechanical problems with equipment.
PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
Maintain fluid levels in hydraulic reservoirs. Maintain equipment filters and change as necessary or per PM schedule. Grease equipment as required or defined in associated instructions. Repair various mechanical issues including, but not limited to, hydraulic, air, or water leaks in a timely manner. Maintain PM of safety devices on equipment.
ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES
Apply knowledge of lockout procedure prior to performing work on equipment. Perform emergency repairs and preventive maintenance as scheduled. Participate, as needed, in internal problem solving/improvement activities. Input, read, and complete work orders. Maintain forklift maintenance check list. Other duties as assigned by supervision. OTHER REQUIREMENTS
Associates degree or equivalent from 2-year college or technical school or a minimum of 1 year of related experience. All employees are responsible for complying with the safety policies and procedures. Ability to work in a fast-paced environment. Ability to effectively communicate with all levels of associates. Ability to actively participate in problem solving activities. Ability to carry up to 75 lbs. and torque up to 180 lbs. Perform basic math functions – addition, subtraction, multiplications, division, percents, proportions. Able to support overtime during week or weekends.
POSITION KEY INTERFACES
INTERNAL EXTERNAL
Plant Manager/Productions Supervisors/RO/Operators Corporate Manufacturing support Engineers/Quality
KEY MEASURE ACCOUNTABILITY
Safety Problem Solving Quality Teamwork/Interpersonal Skills Company/Plant Measurables
EMPLOYEE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT
